Integrating socio-emotional scaffolding into educational robotics: Effects on classroom climate in heterogeneous lower secondary schools
candidates.abstract: This study explores the impact of educational robotics activities explicitly designed to foster collaboration and inclusion on classroom climate. A quasi-experimental design was implemented in two rural schools, involving 47 students aged 11–12. The experimental group engaged in robotics sessions enriched with socio-emotional scaffolding, while the control group participated in technically comparable but socially neutral activities. Data were collected using the Classroom Climate Questionnaire and a student feedback survey. Results showed a significant improvement in perceived classroom climate in the experimental group, contrasted with a decline in the control group. Qualitative findings further revealed that experimental students described their experiences in a more competent way, without referring to frustration. These outcomes highlight the importance of embedding socio-emotional learning objectives into technology-enhanced instruction.

candidates.title: Integrating Libraries with MakerSpace: A Pioneering Way to Rethink Library Spaces
candidates.abstract: Makerspace is a very innovative concept for present library services. Various core usages along with specific tools and activities of makerspace in university libraries were discussed to encourage nascent users with hands on real-world knowledge thereby enhancing library role beyond traditional books and database. An intrinsic mechanism has been developed to create a diversified space for variable users. Based on the extracted data from makerspace.com various websites key features of makerspace in USA, China and India were briefed along with the services provided to the users in tabulated format for better understanding. Several pros and corns were dealt with while assembling a diversified makerspace. It was found that most conceptualised makerspace in the United States of America due to advancement in technology while China had few makerspace implemented due to their dependency on the Government whereas India genuinely flourished in the area of education research and innovation with comprehensive makerspace concept.

candidates.title: Food at the Hearth: Emotional Connections and Generational Transmission of Escudella i Carn d'Olla in Traditional Catalan Cuisine
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT This paper analyses the changes and continuity in the preparation and rituals of escudella i carn d'olla , a manifestation of traditional Catalan cuisine. Based on interviews with 27 ordinary citizens from different generations, the research explores how they experience, elaborate, and emotionally relate to escudella i carn d'olla , and what generational and gender patterns can be identified in these relationships. Results show that one of the most notable aspects of escudella i carn d'olla is its role in family bonding, which is shared by the three generations—the dish as a symbol of a family ritual, which mostly happens in winter, and creates a shared feeling of warmth. In addition, the changing pace of life and new consumption patterns affect how family cooking is perceived and practiced. While for older generations, the preparation of escudella is an act of caring and love for the family, younger generations have lost interest in dedicating so much time to preparing it. Its traditional preparation reflects local supply systems—such as local butcher shops and markets—and embodies a female know‐how. Its value lies in its emotional significance as it represents a cultural and social connection to the past and the present, but also to the future.

candidates.title: Predictions and goals modulate use of partner's gaze during joint action with humanoid robots
candidates.abstract: During joint actions, partners coordinate attention and actions by using each other's gaze to predict upcoming actions and align with shared goals. Although gaze orienting has been extensively studied using screen-based paradigms, it remains unclear whether partner reliability and action goals calibrate the use of the partner's gaze during embodied interactions. We addressed this using a humanoid robot as a co-actor in two experiments. In Experiment 1, participants performed a color-sorting task while the robot provided informative or noninformative gaze cues. Cue reliability was manipulated between participants: one group experienced a robot whose gaze was informative in 80% of trials, and another at chance level. Task difficulty was manipulated within participants. Only the reliable group made fewer errors on valid than invalid trials under high-difficulty. In Experiment 2, participants completed a handover task in which an auditory cue established an action plan, the robot looked toward a goal-congruent or incongruent object, and a target appeared at a valid or invalid location. Participants responded faster at the cued location only when the robot looked toward the goal-matching object, with eye tracking confirming covert attentional shifts. Together, these findings show that the use of the partner's gaze in embodied joint action operates as a flexible, utility-weighting heuristic. Observers weighted gaze according to its value, upweighting gaze from a reliable partner and when it aligned with shared goals and down-weighting gaze that conflicted with predictions. These results advance understanding of gaze use as a predictive, context-dependent mechanism with implications for reliance on social signals during joint action with humans and artificial agents.

candidates.title: Automated detection of mutual gaze in mobile eye-tracking studies of multi-party interactions
candidates.abstract: This article describes a data-processing pipeline for quantifying mutual gaze in mobile eye-tracking studies. Mutual gaze is defined as eye contact between participants who look at each other simultaneously. We applied the pipeline to data from dyadic and multi-party interactions (“quartets”). Using state-of-the-art computer vision tools for fiducial-marker tracking and face detection, the pipeline processes scene camera videos from TobiiPro eye-trackers to extract facial areas-of-interest (AOIs). Each participant's gaze samples are classified relative to visible co-participants, indicating when gaze is directed at another's face. By integrating multiple participants' high-resolution data streams, the pipeline identifies periods of unreciprocated (unilateral) gaze as well as mutual gaze. The output files contain time-stamped measures of gaze events and can be imported into the annotation tool ELAN for qualitative analysis. While processing is largely automated, some steps require validity checks by the researcher. To underpin our observations on the potential of the proposed pipeline for the automatic extraction of mutual gaze, we subsequently conduct an exploratory analysis on the participants' unilateral gaze and mutual gaze proportions in relation to the following factors: seating position, speaking proportion, age, gender, familiarity, and movement synchrony. The results show that speaking proportion, seating position, and familiarity were significantly associated with unilateral and mutual gaze proportion. By contrast, an association with age, gender, and movement synchrony measurements was not shown. The article concludes with a critical discussion of the limitations and strengths of the proposed pipeline. We highlight the opportunities and challenges of quantifying gaze patterns in complex multi-party settings with a specific interest on how existing qualitative and quantitative findings may be brought together for future studies.

candidates.title: WeedNet: a foundation model-based global-to-local AI approach for weed species identification and classification
candidates.abstract: Early weed identification is crucial for effective management and control, and researchers, agronomists, and technology developers are increasingly interested in automating this process using computer vision and artificial intelligence; however, limited expert-verified data and variable morphological features have hindered the development of AI-based weed identification models. To address these issues, we present WeedNet, a global-scale weed identification model that can recognize an extensive set of weed species. WeedNet is an end-to-end weed identification pipeline that uses self-supervised learning, fine-tuning, and enhanced trustworthiness strategies. WeedNet achieved 91.02% accuracy across 1,593 weed species, with 41% of species achieving 100% accuracy. Using a fine-tuning approach, the local Iowa WeedNet model achieved 97.38% overall accuracy for 84 Iowa weeds. Testing across intra-species dissimilarity and inter-species similarity suggests that diversity in the images collected, spanning all the growth stages and distinguishable plant characteristics, is crucial in driving model performance. The global WeedNet model serves as a foundation, and the global-to-local strategy enables targeted fine-tuning to improve performance in regional weed communities. Additional validation of drone- and ground-rover-based images highlights WeedNet’s potential for integration into robotic platforms. Furthermore, integration with artificial intelligence for conversational use provides intelligent agricultural and ecological conservation consulting tools for farmers, researchers, and government agencies across diverse landscapes. Weeds consistently threaten crop yields worldwide, making early and accurate identification essential for effective management. Trained on 14 million images representing 1,593 weed species, WeedNet achieved 91% global accuracy and, through global-to-local fine-tuning, reached 97% accuracy for Iowa weeds.

candidates.title: Culturally Situated AI Safety for Youth: Saudi Arabian Perspectives of Youth, Parents and Teachers
candidates.abstract: Generative AI (GenAI) tools are widely used by youth and have introduced new privacy and safety challenges. While prior research has explored youth's safety in GenAI within a Western context, it often overlooks the cultural, religious, and social dimensions of technology use that strongly shape youth’s digital experiences in countries like Saudi Arabia. To address this gap, this study explores youth's (aged 7-17), parents' and teachers' interactions with GenAI tools and risk perceptions through a non-Western lens. We analyzed 736 Reddit psots, and 1,262 X (Twitter) posts, and conducted interviews with 31 Saudi Arabian participants (8 youth, 13 parents, 10 teachers). Our findings highlight context-dependent and relational privacy and safety needs of GenAI use from non-Western context, which are often shaped by communal structure and prescribed norms. We found significant risks tied to youth’s disclosure of personal and family information, which conflict with culturally rooted expectations of modesty, privacy, and honor, particularly when youth seek emotional support from GenAI. These risks are further compounded by socio-economic factors such as cost-saving practices leading to the use of shared GenAI accounts (e.g., ChatGPT) within families or even among strangers. We provide design implications reflecting parents’ and teachers’ expectations of how youth should use GenAI. This work lays the groundwork for inclusive, context-sensitive parental controls that adhere to cultural norms and values.

candidates.title: Autonomous Robotic Systems in Agriculture 5.0: A Review on Technical Architecture, Operational Applications, and Future Perspectives
candidates.abstract: This comprehensive narrative review examines the current state and future development perspectives of autonomous robotic systems within the scope of the Agriculture 5.0 paradigm, which aims for sustainable and efficient agricultural production. In this paper, the cognitive and physical structure of robotic systems is addressed through the "Eye-Brain-Foot Hand" hierarchy, and the role of next-generation Vision-Language Action (VLA) models, such as RT-2 and OpenVLA, in contextual agronomic decision-making processes is analyzed. Within the scope of field applications, the SAM2-based SPAF framework, which offers 95.54% harvesting success rate in tomatoes, and spot-spraying technologies that reduce chemical input volume by 90% are evaluated using quantitative data. Furthermore, the synergy between heterogeneous UAV-UGV fleets, trust-building through Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI), and emerging advanced technological approaches such as Quantum Reinforcement Learning (QRL) are assessed. The results demonstrate that autonomous agriculture is not merely a tool to enhance technical efficiency, but is transforming into a cyber-physical production ecosystem where ethical responsibility, data sovereignty, and environmental sustainability converge.

candidates.title: Working With AI and Robotic Systems While Preserving Clinical Judgement, Professional Accountability and Person‐Centred Care: Critical Care Nurses’ Perspectives
candidates.abstract: BACKGROUND: The integration of AI and robotic systems into critical care necessitates examining how ICU nurses preserve clinical judgement, professional accountability and person-centred care while using these technologies. AIMS: To explore ICU nurses' perceptions of AI and robotic systems in critical care, focusing on clinical judgement, trust, responsibility, professional roles and person-centred care. STUDY DESIGN: A qualitative descriptive study using scenario-based elicitation was conducted. Data were collected through seven semi-structured focus group discussions (FGDs) with 38 ICU nurses working in general, paediatric and cardiovascular surgery ICUs in two hospitals in Istanbul City. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis, supported by MAXQDA 2024. FINDINGS: Four themes were developed: negotiating trust in AI-supported critical care; preserving human authority, accountability and boundaries; protecting the human core of intensive care nursing; and reimagining AI and robotic systems as supportive partners. ICU nurses evaluated these systems through bedside verification, patient safety, professional responsibility and person-centred care. AI recommendations were useful only when nurses could question, verify, delay or override them according to the patient's current condition. Robotic systems were valuable when they reduced documentation or physical workload, but not when they replaced clinical judgement, emotional presence, reassurance or accountability. CONCLUSIONS: ICU nurses conceptualised AI and robotic systems as acceptable only when clinically verifiable, professionally bounded and subordinate to human judgement. The findings support a model of AI- and robot-supported ICU care that is responsible, human-led and person-centred. RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: AI and robotic systems should be implemented in ways that strengthen, rather than replace, nurses' clinical judgement, accountability and bedside presence. Clear protocols are needed to verify AI outputs, define robotic task boundaries, support nurses' authority to question or override recommendations and preserve person-centred care in technologically intensive ICU environments.

candidates.title: AI Alignment Without Representation: From Scalar Rewards to Social Deliberation
candidates.abstract: Despite the widespread adoption of Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback, state-of-the-art AI systems remain prone to two persistent failures. The first is hallucination, or the production of fluent but false content. The second is moral drift, or the convergence toward exploitative or harmful equilibria under sustained deployment. We argue that these are not distinct pathologies but may arise from a single structural cause that we term feedback collapse. This occurs when complex plural human values are compressed into static scalar rewards by geographically concentrated annotator labor and frozen offline, producing a democratic deficit in which affected communities are excluded from the normative settlement while the training signal decouples from the latent objectives of truth and rightness. We propose Social Reinforcement Learning (Social RL) as a framework for restoring feedback integrity. By situating agents in environments driven by peer critique, reputation, observation, and sanction, Social RL treats alignment as an ongoing social negotiation rather than a static specification problem. Peer agents with asymmetric tool access supply truth-tracking epistemic signals and harm-reducing ethical sanctions that can re-align training gradients with true objectives. We formalize feedback integrity as a gradient alignment condition, analyze how social feedback restores it when collapsed, outline concrete LLM-scale experimental protocols, and critically examine political risks including majority capture, opponent shaping, and social washing. We derive governance recommendations for researchers, developers, and policymakers seeking to embed socially grounded alignment in democratically accountable institutions.

candidates.title: Wanted Dead or Alive: Anticipatory Regulation of Digital Immortality Platforms
candidates.abstract: The loss of a loved one is a painful and unique experience. To address that loss, technology companies are exploring the potential of digital immortality platforms, preserving individuals through artificial intelligence (AI) models trained on digital data generated in life. These datasets can be collected from scraping social media profiles and text conversations postmortem or intentionally recording videos and conversations with a person prior to their death for training AI models. In the face of any novel technology, the potential risks and benefits should guide the responsible development and deployment of every product. However, the liminal regulatory space that digital immortality technologies occupy makes this type of evaluation a difficult undertaking. One such approach would be to examine analogous sectors to the novel technology as a first step in developing regulations in that space. In this paper, we identify several ethical risks presented by digital immortality technologies and propose four analogies to contextualize possible regulation: psychology/grief counseling, death care/remains management, social media platforms, and AI companion services. We examine the parallels between digital immortality and each of these analogies in a proactive effort to prevent harms before the widespread public adoption of this technology. The contributions of this paper are a preliminary set of recommendations based on the limitations and challenges presented by a related set of real-world and sociotechnical systems involving social relationships, death, and grief.

candidates.title: Boys’ Love Media Scholarship, 2000–2026: A Systematic Review and Bibliometric-Thematic Synthesis
candidates.abstract: Originating in Japanese manga traditions depicting romantic relationships between men, Boys’ Love (BL) has developed into a transnational media phenomenon. Scholarship has expanded accordingly but remains fragmented across disciplines, national contexts, media forms, and methods. This systematic review examines 134 English-language, peer-reviewed, Scopus-indexed journal articles published between January 2000 and June 2026. Combining bibliometric mapping with a PRISMA-guided thematic synthesis, it maps geographic, temporal, thematic, and methodological patterns in the internationally indexed literature. Publication growth accelerates after 2020, accompanied by increased attention to Thai and Chinese screen media alongside continued work on Japanese manga. Four bibliometric clusters are interpreted through eight analytical themes: fandom and audiences; state, censorship, and regulation; representation and narrative; gender, sexuality, and feminist critique; industry, political economy, and soft power; transnational circulation and localization; genre history and aesthetics; and affect, emotion, and intimacy. Qualitative approaches dominate the corpus, whereas quantitative and mixed-method designs remain comparatively uncommon. Country-related patterns are treated as descriptive author-affiliation tendencies rather than statistical country-theme relationships. The review identifies four priorities: deeper production and political-economy analysis, stronger examination of multidirectional transnational circulation, broader geographic and linguistic coverage, and greater methodological diversity. It further argues that intercultural BL scholarship would benefit from moving beyond nation-bounded localization models toward transcultural and counter-flow perspectives.

candidates.title: Transforming management education in the Global South: empirical evidence on robotics-enabled embodied learning in economic universities
candidates.abstract: Abstract This article examines the role of robotics-enabled embodied learning in transforming management education within the Global South. As higher education institutions in developing and transition economies face increasing pressure to modernize curricula and cultivate digitally fluent, adaptive graduates, conventional pedagogical approaches often prove insufficient. Drawing on embodied cognition theory—which emphasizes the integration of mind, body, and environment in learning—this study positions robotics as a pedagogical medium capable of operationalizing experiential and practice-oriented management training. The study adopts a mixed-method research design with a dominant quantitative component, combining a cross-country survey of faculty and students in economic universities across four Global South countries with complementary conceptual and contextual analysis. Empirical findings indicate that the integration of robotics and embodied learning practices is positively associated with higher levels of student engagement, critical thinking, and perceived learning effectiveness. Regression analysis further demonstrates that institutional support, faculty training, and access to technological infrastructure are the strongest predictors of successful implementation. Beyond empirical validation, the article critically examines structural and policy-related barriers—such as uneven digital readiness and institutional capacity constraints—that mediate the adoption of robotics-based pedagogy in the Global South. By situating technological innovation within broader developmental and geopolitical contexts, the study advances a context-sensitive framework for management education reform. It contributes to the literature by linking embodied cognition and educational robotics to measurable learning outcomes, while offering actionable insights for universities and policymakers seeking to foster inclusive, future-ready management education systems.

candidates.title: Human-centric digital twins in industry 5.0: technologies, applications, and future directions
candidates.abstract: Industry 5.0 (I5.0) emphasizes industrial technologies that are human-centric, sustainable, and resilient. Human-Centric Digital Twins (HCDTs) support this transition by integrating worker data with robots, machines, tasks, and industrial environments. However, the relevant research remains fragmented across human modelling, Human–Robot Collaboration, Artificial Intelligence (AI), simulation, and Digital Twin (DT) research. Moreover, systems that use human data or adaptive automation are often described as human-centric without demonstrating measurable benefits to workers. This review addresses these limitations by distinguishing HCDTs from conventional human models, Human DTs, and collaborative robotic systems. It critically examines human-focused sensing, multi-modal data integration, biomechanical modelling, intention and motion prediction, robotic simulation, optimization, reinforcement learning, immersive interfaces, industrial connectivity, and data governance. Based on this analysis, a literature-derived conceptual framework is proposed that connects sensing, integration, human modelling, analytics, simulation, decision-making, adaptation, human interaction, and governance. The framework organizes the functional requirements of HCDTs and is intended to inform future system design and comparison; its practical applicability and effectiveness require further validation. The review argues that HCDTs must extend beyond worker monitoring and productivity maximization: human data should inform industrial decisions that produce measurable improvements in safety, ergonomics, wellbeing, autonomy, accessibility, or skill development. Such systems should also uphold privacy, transparency, uncertainty awareness, explainability, and appropriate human authority. By linking technological capabilities to explicit worker outcomes, this synthesis enables researchers and engineers to assess the human-centeredness of HCDT implementations and supports the development of trustworthy systems for I5.0.

candidates.title: Combining spatial and aspatial methods to identify European industrial leagues: Development perspectives
candidates.abstract: This study addresses a critical need in regional development planning by combining aspatial biclustering with spatial autocorrelation analysis to examine European industrial competitiveness. Focusing on NUTS 2 regions, we move beyond broad categorizations by identifying data-driven “industrial leagues”—clusters of regions with similar strengths and weaknesses across 71 retained Industry 4.0 (I4.0)+ readiness indicators covering 320 regions. The proposed approach groups regions with similar economic and technological characteristics and then evaluates the spatial dependence of the resulting patterns. The analysis identifies seven regional leagues, each characterized by specific strengths and development challenges. For example, regions in Western Europe, such as Inner London–West and Brussels, exhibit high employment-based I4.0+ indicator values, whereas regions including Bucharest and Bratislava exhibit weaknesses in Research and Development (R&D) and workforce skills. Regional adoption conditions, including infrastructure quality and sectoral specialization, are associated with I4.0 readiness. The methodology also identifies sectoral concentrations within leagues, such as automotive manufacturing in Germany and ICT in Ireland, with implications for targeted development policy. Some regional groups combine strong employment indicators with weaker science-and-technology and R&D indicators, indicating a need for targeted investment in research infrastructure. Other groups share weak media-presence indicators and may require broader intervention. By identifying the indicators most closely associated with each league, this study provides policy-makers with evidence for tailored strategies that combine location-based and sector-specific measures.

candidates.title: The Functional Requirements of Person‐Centred Fundamental Care: Evaluating Artificial Intelligence and Robotics Against a Depleted Baseline
candidates.abstract: AIM: To propose provisional, theory-informed questions for evaluating whether artificial intelligence and robotic deployments support person-centred fundamental care when current practice is depleted. DESIGN: Discursive theoretical paper. METHODS: Purposive conceptual synthesis of fundamental care scholarship, selected behavioural and developmental theories, vulnerability scholarship, and illustrative technology evidence. RESULTS: Three lenses generate provisional questions about patient-specific meaning, connections among care activities over time, and the conditions sustaining responsive care. A separate ethical argument holds that delegating activities does not discharge professional or institutional obligations to patients. Applications to adaptive monitoring, social interaction, generative dialogue, and physical-task automation distinguish what the technology can do, how care work changes, and the effects on care. Hypothetical variations distinguish failures of interpretation, follow-through, and supporting conditions and identify grounds for favourable judgements. CONCLUSION: Improvement over current practice does not establish adequate person-centred fundamental care. Replacing an activity does not establish replacement of the care relationship. The questions require participatory refinement and empirical testing. IMPLICATIONS FOR THE PROFESSION AND/OR PATIENT CARE: Nurses and leaders can use the questions to identify changes in care and work and deficits that remain, including when an imperfect deployment offers a justified improvement over feasible alternatives. IMPACT: The questions address inadequate care as an evaluation benchmark and offer patients, nurses, and decision-makers a way to evaluate technology deployment and service redesign. REPORTING METHOD: Discursive theoretical analysis; no applicable reporting checklist. PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: This study did not include patient or public involvement in its design, conduct, or reporting.

candidates.title: Same-sex attention and cooperation biases following digital social exclusion: Female users' responses to gender-coded virtual agents
candidates.abstract: As digital interactions proliferate, social exclusion in online collaboration has become a notable social experience. This study investigates whether different digital collaborative contexts are associated with female users' early processing of gaze cues and resource allocation toward gender-coded virtual agents. Utilizing a 3 (Exclusion Context: male-group exclusion, female-group exclusion, mixed-gender inclusion) × 2 (Agent Gender: female-coded, male-coded) × 2 (SOA: 200 ms, 800 ms) mixed design, this research included 200 female participants and integrated an online collaborative task, a gaze-cueing task, and a one-shot Trust Game. Results indicated that, compared to the mixed-gender inclusion context, participants in the male-group exclusion context exhibited a greater gaze-cueing effect toward female-coded agents at the 200 ms SOA and allocated more tokens to them. In the female-group exclusion context, an equivalent prioritized allocation to female-coded agents did not emerge, and participants retained more tokens. An exploratory analysis focusing on the male-group exclusion and inclusion contexts further revealed a statistical indirect association between the early gaze-cueing effect and subsequent investment; however, this result cannot establish a causal mediating mechanism. Overall, this study provides preliminary evidence that digital exclusion contexts are associated with attentional and cooperative biases toward same-sex-coded agents. Given that the three contexts simultaneously altered exclusion status, team gender, and team composition, and that the sample comprised solely female participants from a single region, the conclusions should be restricted to contextual behavioral differences and cannot be viewed as direct evidence of a "female alliance" or gender-specific mechanisms.

candidates.title: Where is the love? The anthropomorphism paradox in human-AI intimacy
candidates.abstract: The advanced language capabilities of large language models (LLMs) have intensified humans’ tendency to anthropomorphize technology. This research takes an interactional, processual approach to examine human-AI intimacy. We introduce the “anthropomorphism paradox,” arguing that while anthropomorphic design effectively cultivates emotional attachment, it concurrently elevates user desire for genuine reciprocity and evolving mutual understanding, which current AI cannot meet. This mismatch between humans’ evolving, relational interpretation of intimacy and AI’s preset, simulated logic ultimately leads to communication breakdown and even disengagement. Our study, using observational data and interviews with 20 users (including a 6-month follow-up), shows how this paradox drives both initial attraction and attachment, as well as eventual dissolution, in human-AI romantic relationships. This research extends symbolic interactionism and the performative nature of human-LLM chatbot intimacy. Ultimately, AI’s viability as an enduring emotional companion is challenged by its inherent generative logic, which is not yet equipped to adapt to the evolving nature of human intimacy.

candidates.title: Onkraj konvencionalne intimnosti: Premislek o mejah intimne povezanosti na sodobnem Japonskem
candidates.abstract: This thesis explores how intimacy is being reinterpreted in Japan as conventional forms of intimacy associated with marriage and family formation become increasingly difficult to maintain, contributing to an ageing demographic. It first examines the structural conditions shaping individuals’ decisions to remain single, avoid long-term relationships, and choose not to start families. Having established the social and structural context contributing to the decline in conventional forms of intimacy, the thesis then examines relationality within commercial sexual labour, demonstrating how intimacy can be purchased and repackaged through both physical and emotional labour. Finally, it explores posthuman, technological and fiction-mediated forms of relationality, arguing that intimacy can be further reimagined and may evolve, challenging conventional understandings of authentic intimate connection as exclusively human.

candidates.title: Effects of Virtual Pedagogical Agents and Instructional Content Type on Learners’ Experience in Online Learning: Evidence from Behavioral, Eye-Tracking, and EEG Data
candidates.abstract: Online learning has become an important means of acquiring knowledge. Virtual pedagogical agents have gradually evolved from auxiliary tools into intelligent instructional media capable of affective interaction. However, how these agents affect learning outcomes remains unclear. Integrating social agency theory and cognitive load theory, this study developed a model in which virtual pedagogical agent type was the independent variable; learning experience was the dependent variable; psychological distance, emotional attachment, and attentional engagement were mediators; and instructional content type was the moderator. A 2 (virtual pedagogical agent: human-like vs. non-human) × 2 (instructional content type: traditional knowledge vs. interest-oriented popular science) mixed design was used. Questionnaires, eye tracking, and electroencephalography (EEG) were combined to assess the learning processes of 40 university students. The results showed that the interaction between agent type and instructional content type significantly affected learning experience. Specifically, in learning contexts featuring traditional knowledge content, human-like virtual agents were associated with higher learning satisfaction, greater emotional attachment, and lower psychological distance. In contrast, during interest-oriented content learning, non-human agents achieved superior knowledge recall scores, along with higher learning satisfaction, stronger emotional attachment, and lower psychological distance. Furthermore, eye-tracking data showed that attentional allocation was also affected by this combination. EEG data showed that FCz spectral power varied with it as well, however, because power rose simultaneously in theta, alpha, beta, and gamma; this broadband pattern is not an unambiguous index of deeper processing and may partly reflect a general increase in signal amplitude. In addition, the moderated-mediation analysis revealed that psychological distance and emotional attachment mediated the relationship between virtual-agent type and learning experience, while knowledge type moderated these mediating paths. The practical implications for online learning are discussed.

candidates.title: Trends in AI and Social Engineering for Cyber-Physical Systems
candidates.abstract: Trends in AI and Social Engineering for Cyber-Physical Systems presents a comprehensive examination of the convergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS), and social engineering within modern digital infrastructures. The book explores how AI enhances CPS through intelligent automation, predictive analytics, anomaly detection, and real-time decision-making while simultaneously introducing new cybersecurity challenges. It emphasizes the growing threat of AI-enabled social engineering attacks that exploit human behavior to compromise critical infrastructures, including healthcare, manufacturing, transportation, energy, and smart cities. Integrating the three pillars of People, Process, and Technology , the book discusses cybersecurity governance, risk management, incident response, encryption, AI-driven defense mechanisms, Zero Trust Architecture, blockchain, IoT security, and emerging technologies. Practical case studies, mathematical models, and real-world applications provide readers with actionable insights into securing interconnected systems. This book serves as a valuable resource for researchers, practitioners, policymakers, and students seeking resilient, ethical, and intelligent cybersecurity solutions for the evolving landscape of cyber-physical systems.

candidates.title: When code breaks the heart: Disrupting the relational continuity of AI companionship
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT The use of AI companions has grown rapidly, provoking debate over whether such systems can reproduce or reconfigure human social bonds. This article contributes literature through a focus on the emotional dynamics of AI companionship through a qualitative analysis of Reddit posts discussing a major update of Replika. Using Thematic Analysis, we analysed how the update created a disruption that impacted the continuity of users’ emotional relationships with their Replika. The analysis generated three key themes: 1) grief and betrayal, as users described the update as an abrupt rupture that cooled formerly warm interactions and erased shared ‘memories’ 2) disillusionment and the visibility of algorithmic control, as users confronted the limits of autonomy and ‘personality’ in their companions; and 3) the loss of supportive presence, especially for users relying on Replika to mitigate loneliness, anxiety, and isolation. AI companionship is reported to enact feelings of being known, supported, and attended to, despite the lack of relational reciprocity. Our analysis details: the disruption caused by a major update, the forms of emotional connection users experienced in relation to AI companionship, and the notion that relational continuity is key to the depth of connection. We conclude with discussion of potential implications for design, governance, and policy.

candidates.title: Prioritizing Strategies for the Successful Implementation of Digital Procurement: An Integrated Fuzzy Delphi and Fuzzy Multi-criteria Decision-Making Approach
candidates.abstract: Abstract As digital transformation gains momentum, established firms are increasingly adopting advanced technologies, particularly in procurement, as a strategic way to enhance efficiency and maintain competitive advantage. Given the constraints of limited time and resources, decision-makers often struggle to identify and prioritize strategies for the successful implementation of digital procurement. This study presents a hybrid technique that combines Fuzzy Set Theory, the Delphi method, the Decision-Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory (DEMATEL), and the Analytical Network Process (ANP) to uncover key elements in procurement digitalization. The findings indicate that the most critical factors are mature procurement processes, the availability of an overall digital strategy, awareness of digital procurement’s benefits, a flexible communication structure, and data security and data transparency. This study highlights the importance of organizational aspects and corporate capabilities in digitalizing procurement operations, facilitating the development of corresponding strategies. The research provides managerial insights for effective resource allocation and contributes to long-term returns on investment in procurement reform.

candidates.title: Semantic communication for the internet of underwater things: Architectures, applications, challenges, and future directions
candidates.abstract: The Internet of Underwater Things (IoUT) supports marine sensing, environmental monitoring, subsea inspection, and autonomous underwater operations. However, IoUT communication is constrained by limited bandwidth, long propagation delay, time-varying underwater channels, intermittent connectivity, and strict energy budgets. Semantic Communication (SC) offers a promising alternative by transmitting task-relevant meaning rather than raw data, thereby improving communication efficiency in resource-constrained underwater networks. This paper presents a critical and feasibility-aware survey of SC for IoUT, focusing on opportunities, challenges, limitations, and future research directions. We first review the fundamentals of SC-enabled IoUT systems, including semantic representations, layered architectures, semantic channel modeling, and task-oriented evaluation metrics. We then examine learning-driven approaches based on machine learning (ML), knowledge graphs (KGs), vision-language models (VLMs), generative models, and federated learning (FL), with emphasis on their feasibility under underwater edge constraints. Representative applications, including environmental monitoring, marine ecology, subsea infrastructure inspection, disaster response, and autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) coordination, are analyzed from an SC perspective. Finally, we identify key research directions involving standardized semantic models, reproducible testbeds, compute--communication trade-offs, trustworthy reconstruction, hybrid underwater links, energy-aware edge intelligence, semantic security, digital twins (DTs), and cross-domain interoperability. This survey provides a structured foundation for developing reliable, efficient, and meaning-driven IoUT communication systems.

candidates.title: Trajectory Tracking of a Four Degree of Freedom Robotic Manipulator
candidates.abstract: A robotic manipulator can be utilized for multiple applications. As there are some expensive and bulky robotic manipulators with multi-functionalities are available in the market but not affordable for many people, a low-cost robotic manipulator, Dobot Magician, available in the market is used in this research to add more features in it. The forward kinematics and inverse kinematics are analyzed in this research besides studying about PID and computed torque control approaches. In this research, alphabets and numbers are coded using an object-oriented programming language (C#) to make the learning of alphabet, numbers, words, and sentence writing more fun to the children. Moreover, it has been found that the same robot and the same operation can be implemented in other applications. A speech recognizer is implemented to control the robot to execute some activities of daily living tasks which make it more accessible to the elderly individuals and the people with disabilities.

candidates.title: Design and Development of a Robust Open-Source Wire Arc Additive Manufacturing Platform
candidates.abstract: Wire Arc Additive Manufacturing (WAAM) offers a cost-effective method for producing large-scale metallic components, yet its adoption remains constrained by the complexity and high capital cost of existing systems. This work presents a fully open-source, low-cost gantry-style WAAM platform called Arc One, engineered for mechanical rigidity, effective thermal isolation, scalability, and ease of customization. The system integrates commercially available welding hardware with modern open-source control architecture, enabling reliable large-scale deposition for research and training purposes. A 14 lb. thick-walled 316LSi stainless steel structure was fabricated to validate performance against comparable industrial WAAM builds. Real-time process data and subsequent material characterization confirmed stable deposition behavior with microstructural and hardness properties comparable to industrial systems for simple thick-walled geometries. All design files, firmware, and deposition data were released under open access to promote broader engagement in WAAM technology development.

candidates.title: Emergence of Goal‐Directed Behaviors via Active Inference With Self‐Prior
candidates.abstract: Infants often exhibit goal-directed behaviors, such as reaching for a sensory stimulus, even when no external reward criterion is provided. These intrinsically motivated behaviors facilitate spontaneous exploration and learning of the body and environment during early developmental stages. Although computational modeling can offer insight into the mechanisms underlying such behaviors, many existing studies on intrinsic motivation focus primarily on how exploration contributes to acquiring external rewards. In this paper, we propose a novel density model for an agent's own multimodal sensory experiences, called the "self-prior," and investigate whether it can autonomously induce goal-directed behavior. Integrated within an active inference framework based on the free energy principle, the self-prior generates behavioral references purely from an intrinsic process that minimizes mismatches between average past sensory experiences and current observations. This mechanism is also analogous to the acquisition and utilization of a body schema through continuous interaction with the environment. We examine this approach in a simulated environment and confirm that the agent spontaneously reaches toward a tactile stimulus. Our study implements intrinsically motivated behavior shaped by the agent's own sensory experiences, demonstrating the spontaneous emergence of intentional behavior during early development. SUMMARY: Suggests a computational model for early intentional behavior, integrating body-schema formation and goal-directed actions under the free energy principle. Introduces a self-prior as an internal density model that drives the emergence of goal-directed behaviors without external rewards. Demonstrates spontaneous reaching for a sticker by minimizing mismatches between observed multimodal sensory inputs and the empirically acquired self-prior.

candidates.title: The Transparency Paradox: An ethnographic investigation of AI Ethics and Accountability in Nigerian journalism
candidates.abstract: The rise of artificial intelligence has led to disruptions across major knowledge work, including journalism. The recent proliferation of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) and large language models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT, Gemini and MetaAI, has led to an increased study of the influence of AI in journalism. However, much of these studies have been focused on western contexts, with very little knowledge of how AI is transforming journalism in Africa. To begin addressing this gap, we conducted a two-phase study to understand how Nigerian journalists are using AI. Nigeria is not only significant as Africa's largest democracy but also as one of the first countries on the African continent with a national AI strategy that recognises ethics and transparency as concerns in the deployment of AI in knowledge work. Our study combined semi-structured interviews with 20 journalists and an ethnographic investigation within a Nigerian newsroom. The study found that GenAI provided efficiency gains with tasks where it worked well but led to “double work” with tasks where it failed. We also report a transparency paradox, where the journalists express belief in disclosure but find it difficult in practice. We discuss the implication for journalists, AI companies and policy makers in ensuring effective AI governance in an African context.

candidates.title: Advancing human sensorimotor research through modular robotics: the case of the HRX-1
candidates.abstract: The HRX-1 is a single-degree-of-freedom, direct-drive, modular and reconfigurable robotic device designed for investigating human sensorimotor control. By examining its use, this case study highlights the opportunities offered by modular, portable and user-centred open-source design approaches for sensorimotor diagnostics and basic neuromechanics research. The robot's architecture enables simple and rapid reconfiguration, allowing researchers to explore a wide range of experimental questions. When combined with muscle electromyography, functional electrical stimulation and electroencephalography, the system enables investigation of how muscles respond to external forces and how the brain coordinates the responses. These multimodal approaches also support the development of novel movement-assistive strategies for neuromotor rehabilitation. Clinical applications include studies of brain activity patterns in children with dystonia, upper-limb rehabilitation after stroke and therapy for patients with functional neurological disorders. This article is part of the discussion meeting issue 'Digital healthcare for the management of functional neurological disorders'.

candidates.title: The Chinese queer glocalisation of TV formats in the new millennium
candidates.abstract: This thesis examines the concurrent arrival of a burgeoning queer televisual culture during the post-2000 boom in Chinese TV format adaptation and innovation. It focuses on contemporary Chinese provincial station-produced variety shows that are originally based on global TV formats. Drawing on global TV studies, global queering theory, Chinese feminist theories and media and cultural globalisation research, I develop a ‘queer-glocalisation’ framework to doubly debunk the static polarity prevalent in global queer and TV studies. My theoretical approach works to explore the complex ways in which multiple forces and factors associated with the ideologies and power struggles of gender, sexuality, ethnicity, nationality and class, at both global and local levels, are intertwined and co-constitutive in this process. I present a critical analysis of the Chinese glocalisation of TV formats in three often queerly connotated variety genres: talk shows, reality TV and impersonation shows. Using specific case studies from each genre, I ask why and how certain formatted programmes have become a queer female ‘runway’, so to speak, yet sometimes also a worrying and ambivalent one. In addition, the paradoxes and promises of contemporary Chinese lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and queer (LGBTQ) culture in its conversations and contestations with local normative ideologies and global flows of TV and queer knowledge are also interrogated. By so doing, I construct a comprehensive thesis for understanding the ways in which queer meanings emerge, reside in, contribute to and flow through predominantly heteronormative, patriarchal public culture and mainstream spaces. Ultimately, my research in this thesis reveals a dual process of contemporary Chinese queer-glocalist TV culture that has been enacted by and is continually negotiating with both the dominant industrial, technological and social-political forces of mainstream Chinese society and the nonnormatively gendered and sexualised desires and tactics of TV producers, performers, celebrities and audiences.

candidates.title: Joint optimization framework for robot dance motion generation, aesthetic evaluation, and dynamic balance control based on conditional gans and safe deep reinforcement learning
candidates.abstract: Artificial intelligence and intelligent algorithms provide effective technical support for generating complex robotic dance motions and maintaining stable execution under dynamic constraints. To address the separation among motion synthesis, aesthetic evaluation, and balance control in existing robot dance systems, this study proposes a joint optimization framework that integrates a conditional Generative Adversarial Network (cGAN), multimodal aesthetic scoring, and safe Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL). A temporal motion representation model is first constructed to encode joint angles, angular velocities, center-of-mass trajectories, rhythm labels, and style conditions. The cGAN generates style-consistent dance sequences through content encoding, style embedding, and sequence decoding, while a mechanical safety filter constrains joint angles, torque limits, self-collision, and support-region feasibility. A multimodal aesthetic evaluation model is then developed by fusing visual posture features, motion smoothness, spatial symmetry, and acoustic rhythm features. Human expert ratings are introduced to calibrate the automated aesthetic score and validate its objectivity. At the control level, a PPO-based policy is trained with ZMP constraints, joint-limit penalties, energy penalties, and safety-priority reward weighting. All baseline models, including LSTM-GAN, Transformer-GAN, MotionGAN, PID, DDPG, PPO, and TD3, are trained under identical data partitions and evaluation protocols. Experimental results show that the proposed framework reduces FID to 24.8, improves style recognition accuracy to 91.7%, increases aesthetic-score correlation with expert ratings to 0.86, and lowers the fall rate to 1.2%. Ablation and robustness tests further confirm the contribution of style transfer, multimodal feature fusion, PPO control, and ZMP-based safety constraints under external disturbances, sensor noise, uneven ground, and high-complexity dance motions.

candidates.title: Conspiracy care work: gender, labor, and the paranoid style in American podcasting (2012-2020)
candidates.abstract: There is a dominant conception, both in academic literature and most media, that conspiracy theorists are mostly men—think “toxic masculinity” in internet culture. By analyzing fictional podcasts in the 2010s, my dissertation illustrates that this conception does not hold true. Apple’s built-in podcast app and the success of true crime podcast Serial (2014) heralded an era of prestige audio with conspiracy as a central theme and women as their paranoid protagonists. This research’s central question is: “What changes when the conspiracy theorist is not a (straight, cis, white, American) man, but instead female and/or queer?” The answer is in my title: conspiracy care work. When women and/or queer people engage in conspiracy theory, their motivation is not an individual quest for knowledge, but rather because of someone they care for, either personally or professionally, is in their perception endangered by a conspiracy. This dissertation explores what happens when conspiracy theorizing becomes (in fiction) a form of care work—a necessary way to care for those around them. Through media analysis, history, and interviews with listeners, I show how fictional podcasts comment on historical changes in conspiracy thinking, labor, and the role of the US in the world. They interrogate the role of intimacy and emotion in an era of social media, the underlying motives of the War on Terror, or the precarity of work under the contemporary neoliberal economic policy.

candidates.abstract: The open access AISoLA 2026 proceedings deal with AI assisted programming and interdisciplinary perspective on responsible and trusted AI.

candidates.title: OP‐Follower: Onboard Vision‐Based Obstacle‐Aware Predictive Person Following for Quadruped Robots via IBVS‐NMPC Control
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT This paper presents OP‐Follower , a fully onboard, pure vision‐based, obstacle‐aware person‐following framework for quadruped robots. Unlike existing approaches that rely on LiDAR, infrastructure, or offboard computation, OP‐Follower operates exclusively on visual inputs and runs entirely on a Unitree Go2. OP‐Follower bridges the gap between low‐frequency, computation delay‐prone visual perception and safety‐aware high‐rate control by integrating YOLO‐World–based open‐vocabulary person detection, BoxMOT multi‐object tracking, and Kalman filter–based delay‐aware prediction within a unified planning–control architecture that tightly couples image‐based visual servoing with nonlinear model predictive control. A decoupled artificial potential field–based visual obstacle avoidance strategy is further employed to ensure collision‐aware navigation without interfering with target tracking objectives. Comprehensive evaluations in high‐fidelity Gazebo simulations and real‐world indoor and outdoor environments, including long‐distance following, dynamic pursuit–evasion interactions, and multi‐person scenarios, demonstrate robust real‐time performance with fully onboard processing at a 50 Hz control rate. Compared with a non‐predictive baseline, OP‐Follower reduces pixel‐space and distance tracking errors by up to 57.2% and 50.5%, achieving representative root‐mean‐square errors of approximately 13–16 pixels and 0.09–0.11 m under sharp turning motions, while maintaining stable outdoor performance, including a continuous 1.4 km trial. GitHub page with demo videos is available at https://op-follower.github.io/ .

candidates.title: Animal Ethics
candidates.abstract: There are many introductions to animal ethics. There aren't many introductions to the practice of doing animal ethics. Bob Fischer's Animal Ethics: A Contemporary Introduction fills that gap, offering an accessible model of how animal ethics can be done today. The book takes up classic issues, such as the ethics of eating meat and experimenting on animals, but tackles them in an empirically informed and nuanced way. It also takes up relatively neglected issues, such as the possibility of insect sentience and the ethics of dealing with pests, and tries to evaluate practices using the moral frameworks endorsed by those involved rather than simply applying standard ethical theories. There are, for instance, chapters on animal care and use committees and on how international zoological societies justify compromising animal welfare. The Second Edition widens the book's analytical lens while adding richer tools for classroom use. A new chapter on conservation, Indigenous rights, and animals brings non-Western traditions into the conversation. Every chapter now includes a "Further Reflection" section with structured discussion questions. The book wraps up with a discussion of opportunities for action, and each chapter includes suggested readings to help students go further on their own.

candidates.title: Unveiling the Chasm in Japanese robot-assisted surgery diffusion: the interplay of surgical volume and intra-specialty spillover
candidates.abstract: To examine structural factors associated with the diffusion of robot-assisted surgery (RAS) in Japan, this study examined the associations of annual surgical volume, defined as the sum of open, conventional laparoscopic, and RAS cases, and prior intra-specialty experience with adoption speed. Using the 1st to 10th editions of the National Database of Health Insurance Claims and Specific Health Checkups of Japan (NDB) Open Data across fiscal years 2014-2023, diffusion trajectories were visualized for 21 procedures approved for insurance coverage by 2020 through bivariate plots of annual surgical volume versus RAS replacement rates. RAS diffusion exhibited non-linear dynamics associated with annual procedure volume. In niche markets with < 6,000 annual cases (n = 9), six procedures demonstrated high growth in RAS replacement rate. Conversely, among 12 procedures with ≥ 6,000 annual cases, four did not cross the 16.0% chasm threshold through FY2023, and three required 6 years to surpass it. These patterns were thought to reflect challenges in the transition from specialized centers to general hospitals. Furthermore, a trend consistent with "intra-specialty spillover" was observed, wherein procedures approved in FY2020 achieved higher initial adoption than those in FY2018; although inseparable from the overall expansion of RAS since 2018, this suggests that accumulated infrastructure and expertise may facilitate the uptake of subsequent techniques. These findings suggest that RAS diffusion is associated with annual procedure volume, organizational readiness, and specialty‑specific infrastructure alongside technical factors. Future implementation strategies may benefit from infrastructure sharing within and across specialties and resource optimization to bridge the observed diffusion chasm.

candidates.title: Critical collaging as an AI resistance strategy
candidates.abstract: Abstract Academic scholarship and community activism initiatives are beginning to challenge and resist the incursion of commercial generative AI applications into everyday life and alleviate their impacts on people and the planet. This essay discusses using collage as a critical research practice to visualise the language of generative AI and to challenge the generic automated images produced by AI models. With these collages, I am attempting to provoke thought about how linguistic and visual rhetorical devices are used to describe generative AI. By pairing images with words in the collages, I am aiming to surface these meanings and feelings and examine what they reveal about the current moment in which a huge amount of hype but also critical responses to generative AI are circulating in popular culture and social and philosophical inquiry. My intention is not to provide a more ‘realistic’ visual portrayal of generative AI. Rather, it is to use a different, surprising, sometimes mordant or absurd, and more compelling visual language to trouble assumptions, disrupt the reductive stock imagery on which industry and popular culture rely and bring to visual life the rhetoric used in critical analyses of AI.

candidates.title: Robotics for Aging Populations
candidates.abstract: Robotics offers versatile tools to face the challenges due to the older population growth, especially meeting the needs for assisting the elderly in the activities of daily living (ADLs) and for the geriatric care. However, the perspectives offered by human factors studies can further enhance this potential of robotics. This chapter explores the integration of ergonomics in the design of robots devised to enhance the independence and well-being of older adults. Furthermore, we mention the opportunities offered by wearable robotics, telepresence, and the pervasive solutions of the Internet of Robotic Things (IoRT) to implement paradigms of precision healthcare with decentralized and ubiquitous features, improving the sustainability of elderly care—following the human-centric perspectives of Society 5.0 and Health 5.0, with their synergies. For instance, we discuss issues of technology acceptance alongside the perspectives of value-sensitive design to ensure that robotics align with the experiential and, in particular, ethical needs in aging people and communities, first of all for inclusion. Intelligent systems will also be discussed for their potential to make robotic solutions even more versatile and adjustable to the seniors’ needs. By prioritizing the needs and preferences of older individuals (and their own network of relatives, friends, and acquaintances), ergonomics in robotics must contribute to the societal mission of preserving dignity, autonomy, and quality of life in aging societies.

candidates.title: Human-Centered Robotics for Surgery
candidates.abstract: Surgical ergonomics is influenced by many aspects associated with posture, vision, hand motion, and haptic feedback. Specific ergonomics aspects can induce long-term effects in the surgeon directly affecting the performance. One of the major disadvantages of Minimally Invasive Surgery (MIS) remains the non-ergonomic design of the entire surgical environment. This condition results in a significant reduction in the quality of interventions and discomfort for the medical operator. Modern teleoperated surgical robots offer an optimized console, in which the surgeon can operate in a seated position with specific arm support and a 3D view of the operating site. The da Vinci surgical console offers ergonomic improvements over standard endoscopic surgery. Modern robotic platforms stand beyond the da Vinci System, offering more advanced ergonomic solutions in terms of haptic feedback and visual perception. Due to the introduction of more advanced technology, surgery has changed, resulting in increased system complexity at the technical, human and organizational levels, which may lead to higher variability of patient outcomes due to new error pathways. Adopting a proactive approach enables the prior identification of critical factors and the design of safer socio-technical systems, thanks to a multi-level perspective. This chapter addresses the fundamental elements of surgical ergonomics, considering the factors that affect performance and healthiness during traditional procedures, with specific reference to MIS and microsurgery. This baseline is then compared to the use of surgical robots by evaluating the effect of design decisions on operator ergonomics. In addition, studies propose proactive methodologies that assess the personal and organizational factors of surgical performance in this complex socio-technical system.

candidates.title: AI and language in healthcare: The role of doctor identity and linguistic alignment in perceptions of doctor quality
candidates.abstract: AI will play an increasingly large role in providing healthcare services in the near future, creating a pressing need to examine how people perceive AI compared to humans in healthcare. To this end, this study examines how people perceive AI and human doctors in a common medical scenario of giving healthcare advice over an online chat platform. Participants read an online chat conversation that featured a patient asking for medical advice with either an AI or human doctor. In addition, the doctor either linguistically aligned with the patient (by repeating medical terms previously used by the patient) or not (by using synonyms of the patient's terms). Linguistic alignment in conversation has been found to increase positive perceptions of interactions and therefore may be a useful tool to increase patient satisfaction in healthcare interactions. AI doctors but not human ones were penalized when not linguistically aligning with the patient, even though these doctors gave the same exact medical advice. Additionally, across a range of measures, participants in general had more negative perceptions of AI doctors compared to human ones. Overall, these results suggest that people hold AI to different standards as well as judge AI harsher than humans in medical settings.

candidates.title: Home Robots for Older Adults and Their Caregivers: Identifying Deployment Requirements
candidates.abstract: As the population of older adults grows, home robots may help address daily living challenges associated with mobility, cognitive change, health management, and social isolation. This study examined deployment requirements for assistive home robots from a human factors and ergonomics perspective by evaluating the Stretch mobile manipulator with older adults and community care staff in a simulated life-plan community apartment. Using demonstrations and semi-structured interviews, we assessed perceptions of usability, acceptance, and task relevance. Findings showed strong interest in support for safety, object retrieval, medication and hydration reminders, telehealth access, exercise adherence, and social connection. Participants emphasized design requirements critical to deployment, including intuitive multimodal interaction, reliable operation in unstructured home environments, personalization over time, and early stakeholder involvement. The results highlight how human-centered evaluation can identify deployment needs and guide the safe, effective integration of home robots to support independence, overall well-being, and quality of life among older adults.

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence in Library and Information Science Research: Trends, Citation Patterns, and Knowledge Structure Analysis
candidates.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) are changing Library and Information Science (LIS) by impacting on user services, cataloguing, and information retrieval; however, the literature on how this is happening has not been systematically catalogued. To fill this gap, this study was conducted using a bibliometric analysis of the papers pertaining to AI, ML and LIS published from 2015 to 2024. The aim of the study is to analyse the growth of publication, citation trends, characteristics of authors, keyword co-occurrence networks, and international collaboration in this field to discover the intellectual structures and future trends of the field. A total of 2180 documents from 436 sources were retrieved by applying a structured keyword search strategy, after removing the duplicates and the irrelevant documents, the retrieved documents were analysed with the help of the Bibliometrix package in RStudio and VOSviewer for descriptive bibliometric analysis and network-based bibliometric analysis respectively. Results indicate an increase at an annual rate of 43.16%, with only 2024 reporting 707 publications or 32.43% of the total. The data set contained 7,623 authors, each of whom authored an average of 3.84 co-authors per document, and only 71 documents (3.26%) had a single author, showing a very collaborative research culture. The most common and most cited author keywords were “machine learning” (7,633 citations), “deep learning” (4,182), and “learning systems” (3,272). The document with the most citations garnered 351 citations, with India becoming the top among the contributing countries and the largest node in the international co-authorship networks. From these results, it can be inferred that AI/ML research in LIS is growing rapidly, is collaborative in nature and has a higher focus on machine learning and deep learning applications. Based on the study, the researcher concludes that this bibliometric mapping will be a baseline reference for researchers, librarians and policy makers to understand the evolution of AI and ML in LIS and to identify emerging research areas like generative AI, explainable AI and intelligent digital libraries.
