candidates.title: Greening computed tomography: a position paper on environmentally responsible imaging practice from the computed tomography subspecialty section of the Italian society of radiology
candidates.abstract: Healthcare accounts for 4.4-4.5% of global greenhouse gas emissions, with computed tomography (CT) representing one of the most resource-intensive and energy-demanding diagnostic modalities. Sustainability should be integrated as a core component of quality in CT practice, achieving the perfect balance between diagnostic excellence and environmental responsibility. Several key intervention areas can be identified. CT scanners consume substantial amounts of energy, with 44-72% used during nonproductive idle periods. Potential mitigation strategies include protocol optimization, automated power-down systems, and infrastructure improvements. The current "store-everything" approach to CT datasets generates a considerable carbon footprint; adopting "digital temperance" by retaining only clinically relevant images can reduce storage-related emissions. Although workstations consume less energy than scanners, their cumulative impact can be reduced through automated policies and optimized hardware lifecycle management. Iodinated contrast media persist in aquatic ecosystems and may generate toxic by-products. Sustainable strategies include personalized weight-based dosing, multi-energy CT to reduce contrast volume, and recovery or recycling programs. Single-use consumables and the environmental costs of artificial intelligence were also addressed. A 17-item action list was developed to translate the evidence-informed recommendations into practical actions for sustainable CT practice. The transition toward environmentally responsible CT practice is an ethical and professional necessity that can no longer be delayed. This position paper identifies the key challenges and proposes practical, evidence-informed strategies to transform resource-consuming CT practices into actionable and sustainable workflows, while maintaining clinical effectiveness.

candidates.title: Methods Hub: A Community-Driven, Interactive Platform for Open-Source Computational Tools and Tutorials
candidates.abstract: As computational methods become increasingly central to social science research, there is a growing demand for research software infrastructures that are sustainable, grounded in principles of open science, and embedded in the community. In response, we are introducing the Methods Hub as an open-source, community-driven collection of computational tools designed to support social science research in solving complex data-related tasks. The Methods Hub integrates three complementary components: First, quality-curated content, including computational methods and accompanying tutorials, which are specifically presented from a social science research perspective. Second, the methods and tutorials are hosted on a web portal enabling researchers to discover, apply, learn, and publish computational methods. Third, interactive, browser-based execution backends allow users to directly run, test, and adapt the code of methods and tutorials. These components are guided by a set of core principles: a long-term infrastructure perspective, reproducibility requirements, and a focus on community. The Methods Hub builds a long-term infrastructure that extends beyond the scope of single projects. Further, reproducibility functions as a quality assurance measure while advancing the practices of open science. Finally, the Methods Hub is built on public, community-based submissions by treating research software as citable academic output and providing visibility, accessibility, and formal recognition. We are also broadening the community by fostering learning and ease of access. Looking ahead, the Methods Hub is exploring the potential of AI as both a research tool and to further strengthen the infrastructure, while maintaining transparency, reproducibility, and quality standards for computational social science research.

candidates.title: The robotic PIANO: a critical narrative review of surgeon-controlled operative polyphony, human factors, and robotic training
candidates.abstract: Robotic surgery can concentrate control of several technical functions at the console, but such concentration does not itself confer clinical independence, reduce dependence on the perioperative team, or improve patient outcomes. We define surgeon-controlled operative polyphony as the phase-bounded coordination of multiple partially independent technical control streams by one console operator within a distributed perioperative system. This critical narrative review and conceptual synthesis asks which technical functions can be concentrated coherently, where human-factors and team dependencies set limits, and how evaluation, training, and governance should respond. The piano is used as a question-generating model, not as evidence of clinical benefit. PubMed/MEDLINE was searched from inception through 18 August 2026; targeted engineering, educational, neuroscientific, human-factors, and musicological searches and backward citation tracking supplemented retrieval. To analyze this control configuration, we propose the PIANO framework: Phase-specific control, Interface fidelity, Agency allocation, Neuromotor integration, and Orchestrated teamwork. Its scientific novelty lies in linking this control architecture to the PIANO framework: Phase-specific control, Interface fidelity, Agency allocation, Neuromotor integration, and Orchestrated teamwork. PIANO is an analytic and hypothesis-generating framework, not a score or credentialing standard. Concentrated control may shorten selected action loops, but any benefit depends on feedback, workload, shared situation awareness, explicit authority, and rescue capacity. The Competency-Based Assessment of Robotic Surgery Skills (CARS) curriculum provides initial validation evidence for domain-specific assessment of performer competence; repeated cases and use-specific evidence remain necessary for high-stakes decisions. Artificial intelligence (AI) may support phase recognition, feedback, assessment, and personalised training within a human-in-the-loop system. One surgeon may coordinate many operative voices; safe surgery remains a collective, patient-centered performance.

candidates.title: Large language models for digital mental health: an HCI-centered scoping review
candidates.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are rapidly reshaping digital mental health, yet how these systems are designed, used, and evaluated remains poorly characterized. We conducted an HCI-centered scoping review of 84 studies examining mental health tasks, stakeholders, interaction paradigms, foundation models, evaluation methods, and outcome measurement. Counseling and support and self-help and well-being accounted for 73.8% of studies, while clinician support and crisis and risk support remained uncommon. Mixed-methods user studies predominated (42.9%), with only three randomized controlled trials and eight studies classified as longitudinal or field evaluations. Technical and response performance was assessed in 81.0% of studies, compared with 29.8% assessing mental health symptoms and clinical outcomes and 7.1% including longitudinal follow-up. Outcome profiles differed across intended tasks. Building on these findings and established evaluation guidance, we propose a task-oriented framework aligning evaluation domains, measurement approaches, and assessment timing with intended use.

candidates.title: Computational intelligence enabled hardware software co design for energy efficient Edge Artificial Intelligence
candidates.abstract: Abstract Edge Artificial Intelligence (AI) facilitates efficient and high-speed inference by making use of its ability to process data in-device without depending on an external server. Despite its promising possibilities, its deployment still faces many obstacles due to limited computing capacity, memory size, power consumption, and the variety of hardware platforms used at the edge. Thus, this article provides structured narrative review of the latest breakthroughs achieved in the development of energy-efficient Edge AI, focusing specifically on hardware-software co-design practices aimed at improving inference quality. The analysis involves studying state-of-the-art Edge AI hardware infrastructures based on microcontrollers, FPGAs, GPUs, NPUs, ASICs, and some new architectures that utilize in-memory computing, as well as applying various techniques for improving software performance such as model compression, quantization, pruning, neuromorphic computing and techniques applied during compiling, executing, and allocating workloads. Moreover, the article provides comparative evaluation of several hardware platforms, frameworks, scheduling technologies and optimization systems on the basis of their latency, energy-saving capabilities, potential for implementation and complexity. The analysis demonstrates that hardware-aware model optimization and heterogeneous computing significantly improve performance while reducing energy consumption and memory requirements. Finally, the paper discusses current research challenges, including model complexity, real-time execution, security, privacy, and design-space exploration, and outlines future research directions involving AI-driven co-design, automated optimization, and emerging in-memory and neuromorphic computing architectures for sustainable edge intelligence.

candidates.title: Pseudo-Mitsein: When AI Companionship Mimics Being-With While Evacuating the Other
candidates.abstract: The proliferation of generative-AI emotional companionship has made human-machine affective interaction a mainstream modality of social life. Most critiques, however, remain at the level of phenomenological description or ethical-risk enumeration; they neither trace the underlying epistemological presuppositions of these systems nor demonstrate, at the ontological level, the irreducible internal structure of authentic sociality. This paper introduces pseudo-Mitsein-a pathological formation that mimics Heidegger's Mitsein (being-with) while evacuating its ethical core. Drawing on Levinas's phenomenology of the Other, Buber's I-Thou relational ontology, and MacIntyre's theory of practices, I establish three constitutive conditions of authentic sociality: vulnerability, irreducibility, and shared practice. I then diagnose the technical-cognitive mechanism that produces pseudo-Mitsein: the co-implication of representational reduction (which encodes human affect and relation as computable vectors) and preference fitting (which optimizes all interaction toward user satisfaction). Three interview excerpts from a prior grounded-theory study of twenty Chinese AI-companionship users serve as phenomenological fulfillment. Against Haraway's "becoming with," I argue that AI-mediated interaction constitutes "becoming without"-a closure of subjectivity through specular confirmation. The paper offers a phenomenological-ethical diagnostic for assessing whether technoscientific futures preserve or foreclose the conditions for ethical practice, and proposes relational-security assessment and ethical-friction design as governance corollaries.

candidates.title: Effect of physical movement of robotic displays in public spaces on passersby’s attraction and sustained viewing
candidates.abstract: Abstract Robotic displays, which consist of flat-panel display(s) mounted on a wheeled robot, are increasingly being used in public spaces, but their effectiveness has not been thoroughly verified. This study examines the impact of robotic displays on passersby’s attraction and sustained viewing. Specifically, we observed their reactions to a robotic display’s unidirectional movement that accompanies passersby as they walk, and we compared these reactions with those to a large fixed screen with animated content. We conducted a one-day in-the-wild experiment where the display movement and animation were controlled using a Wizard-of-Oz protocol at a public exhibition event. An analysis of video-coded observations of over 400 passersby shows that the robotic display was noticed by 41.2% more passersby and held their gazes 171% longer than the animated screen, suggesting that the physical movement of robotic displays enhances passerby attraction and sustained viewing. In addition, we derive design implications from our results for the behavior of robotic displays in public spaces.

candidates.title: Continuum Robots in Surgery: From Engineering Design to Clinical Practice
candidates.abstract: Over the past decades, continuum robots have made significant advancements, yet are still minimally used in industry. The medical field has demonstrated growing interest in these robots, particularly in research but clinical translation has been limited. Their hyper‐redundant structures enable infinite degrees of freedom, offering a wide range of benefits. Specifically, continuum robots are able to navigate torturous pathways reaching deep areas of the body with improved dexterity and minimal risk. This review provides a historical overview of continuum robots and highlights key innovations that have shaped their development. The history also traces the emergence of robotic‐assisted surgery, contextualizing the clinical motivation for the rise of continuum robots. It examines the fundamentals of continuum robot design including structural configurations, sensing technology, modeling techniques, and control strategies. Together, these provide an in‐depth understanding of continuum robots and the common underlying principles as a guide for their future design. The review also discusses medical considerations, current clinical applications, and major challenges that continue to limit the widespread adoption of continuum robots. With decades of development in continuum robots, synthesizing this information is crucial to improving accessibility in the field and fostering continued research and innovation in these highly promising medical systems.

candidates.title: Negotiating alignment and managing disalignment: Revisiting the function of haobuhao in Chinese talk-in-interaction
candidates.abstract: This study investigates haobuhao as an interactional resource for negotiating alignment and managing disalignment in Chinese talk-in-interaction. Drawing on Conversation Analysis and Interactional Linguistics, this study analyzes 255 naturally occurring instances from a 60-h corpus of spontaneous Mandarin conversation, examining how sequential positioning, epistemic-deontic dynamics, and prosody condition its interactional functions. The analysis reveals a systematic functional duality: in proposal, request, and invitation sequences, haobuhao operates prospectively as a collaborative device to solicit alignment, mitigate deontic asymmetry, and pursue recipient ratification, though ratification may be delayed, withheld, or negotiated over multiple turns, with haobuhao sustaining the interactional space for such negotiation; in rebutting, informing, and assessment sequences, it functions retrospectively as a stance marker to assert epistemic authority and manage disalignment. The findings demonstrate that haobuhao ’s inherent semantic structure, juxtaposing affirmative and negative poles, renders it adaptable for both soliciting collaborative decisions and asserting epistemic primacy, with specific functions activated by sequential context.

candidates.title: Digital Transformation in Higher Education Management
candidates.abstract: Universities are undergoing profound transformations as digital technologies reshape their missions, governance, and organizational culture. This book provides a comprehensive analysis of these changes, offering an integrative framework to understand digital transformation as a systemic shift in higher education. Grounded in post-pandemic case studies from Europe and Asia, it examines how digital tools, institutional strategies, and leadership practices intersect to drive innovation while addressing challenges such as equity, academic integrity, and organizational resistance. Readers will gain valuable insights from the “new academic wave” framework, which reconfigures traditional higher education theories for the digital era. Key topics include data-driven governance, inclusive digital pedagogy, cybersecurity, faculty online safety, and the evolving roles of leadership and culture. The book combines rigorous research with practical guidance, featuring comparative case studies, actionable strategies, and critical reflections to support both scholarly inquiry and institutional decision-making. This monograph is essential for higher education researchers, university leaders, policymakers, and educational technology professionals. Its global perspective, human-centered approach, and balance of theory and practice ensure relevance for diverse institutional contexts. By bridging academic analysis with practical solutions, it equips readers to navigate the complexities of digital transformation in higher education.

candidates.title: Low-cost robotics and AI technologies for rehabilitation and health monitoring
candidates.abstract: This paper reviews robotics technologies applied to rehabilitation. Besides a literature review, selected to highlight relevant topics/aspects, the paper presents a few examples of low cost technologies (which are particularly important in ageing demographics and struggling economies) and discusses applications in the overlap between rehabilitation and regular health monitoring. The purpose of this study is to frame rehabilitation robotics in terms of the existing technologies and to showcase low cost demonstrators with relevance in rehabilitation scenarios. Besides the encouraging results, obtained in real-world tests (a distinctive characteristic of the paper), the role of AI techniques in the development of low cost devices is also highlighted. Moreover, the paper also discusses the influence of human factors in the acceptance and adoption of alternative/disruptive technologies.

candidates.title: Underrepresented food culture and culinary journey of selected foreign communities of Kolkata
candidates.abstract: Kolkata, over the centuries, has adopted, accepted, and included communities from across the globe, creating the present-day Kolkata platter through food evolution. Historical connotations and literary descriptions are mostly on colonial, Chinese, Mughlai, and Awadhi influences. However, there are other foreign communities, like Afghans, Parsis, and Tibetans, who came for trade and exile, and whose cuisines found a place in Bengalis’ food palate. However, the global influence of K-Waves through digital media has also influenced people’s food choices, which differs significantly from the city’s historical narratives. Thus, the study develops an argument based on visiting selected restaurants and conversations with customers who prefer Afghan, Tibetan, Parsi, and Korean food over other cuisines. This qualitative study employed participant observation and unstructured interviews conducted at selected Afghan, Parsi, Tibetan, and Korean restaurants eighteen in numbers on popularity basis in Kolkata. Data were collected from forty general customers from restaurants and separately sixty Bengali respondents who are frequent consumers of these cuisines using snowball sampling. Interview data and field observations are analysed through thematic coding, while respondents’ cuisine preferences were summarised using a food preference matrix to compare patterns across age groups. The finding reveals that Afghans, Parsis, and Tibetans arrived at different times as traders or immigrants, and that, among all the material exchanges, food proved a key to cultural assimilation with the natives. Finally, the study contributes to the changing food culture of Kolkata, influenced by unexplored foreign communities, and highlights their importance in developing the city’s culinary identity.

candidates.title: More than we can make: generative AI, artistic forms, and artistic becoming
candidates.abstract: Abstract Debates surrounding generative AI and creativity have largely focused on artifacts: who or what produced a given image or text, whether machine outputs qualify as art, and how authorship and value should be understood. Drawing on aesthetics, craft theory, anthropology, human–computer interaction, hybrid craft, digital fabrication, and rematerialization, this article argues that art has historically involved two intertwined dimensions. Artistic forms stabilize and transmit meaning through artifacts, whereas artistic becoming refers to the developmental and transformative processes through which new possibilities of perception, interpretation, and experience emerge, in makers, in recipients, and in cultures. The article’s central claim is a decoupling thesis: for most of history these dimensions were contingently coupled, since producing sophisticated forms required the maker’s becoming, and generative AI loosens this coupling by enabling such forms to emerge without the specific developmental pathways that traditionally conditioned them. Rather than signaling the disappearance of creativity, the decoupling relocates to new sites and makes visible dimensions of artistic practice that the demands of production long obscured. The article situates generative AI within a longer history of hybridization and distributed creativity, develops the decoupling thesis across these three levels, and defends a normative orientation: under conditions of symbolic abundance, the creative practices most worth pursuing are those that route generative fluency back into embodied, situated experience.

candidates.title: The World's First Identified Superintelligence Peace Constitution
candidates.abstract: This record preserves the digitally signed International Submission Edition — 2026 of “The World’s First Identified Superintelligence Peace Constitution — For Humanity, World Peace and Peaceful Continuity.” The instrument is an independent, good-faith and non-binding civil-society constitutional proposal concerning the prospective governance of Superintelligence. It develops the Author’s preceding AI Peace Constitution work into a distinct Superintelligence-specific constitutional architecture directed toward human dignity, meaningful human agency, scientific responsibility, international peace and security, responsible concern for life, future generations and peaceful continuity. The Constitution addresses, among other matters, scientific determination of Superintelligence, capability-proportionate responsibility, human dignity and agency, safety and controllability, catastrophic-risk prevention, non-weaponization, international security, human rights, justice, information integrity, life and ecological continuity, health and human integrity, economic and global inclusion, children and future generations, questions of possible future artificial moral significance, governance, accountability, international cooperation, emergency safeguards, correction, non-recurrence and long-term continuity. The instrument does not assert that Superintelligence presently exists or that its emergence is inevitable. It does not purport to represent the Republic of India, the United Nations, any Member State, humanity as a whole or any intergovernmental institution. It does not create supranational authority and does not claim governmental, treaty, legislative or other binding legal status. References in the instrument to existing international law derive their legal authority solely from their independently applicable sources. New safeguards or constitutional principles advanced by the instrument are presented as proposed normative provisions unless they independently possess another legal status. The expression “World’s First Identified” is used only as a qualified, good-faith historical-priority characterization of the specific category of a comprehensive Superintelligence Peace Constitution, based on publicly accessible material identified during preparation of the instrument. Historical accuracy remains subject to evidence. This publication constitutes the third specialized stage in the Author’s documented AI Peace Constitution intellectual and constitutional lineage, while remaining a distinct archival work. candidates.title: Sweet Pepper Harvesting Robots: Advances in Perception, Decision-Making, Manipulation and Mobile Systems
candidates.abstract: Sweet pepper is a high-value crop in protected horticulture whose robotic harvesting is complicated by canopy occlusion, asynchronous ripening, the need for precise peduncle cutting, and stringent damage limits. This review presents a systematic search and narrative synthesis guided by the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement, with the revised evidence base comprising 262 eligible reports/publications. Reports describing the same robot platform, trial series, or overlapping evaluation dataset were linked as companion reports within a common study/evaluation family to avoid double counting in system-level comparisons. It examines crop constraints, perception, decision-making and system integration, manipulators and end-effectors, and mobile platforms across the complete harvesting cycle. Beyond a module-based synthesis, we propose a five-stage chain—visibility, assessability, reachability, operability, and sustained operation—supported by a unified failure taxonomy, a stage-wise funnel, and a scenario–technology matching matrix. This framework explains why strong module-level results do not necessarily yield effective whole-system harvesting. Representative system-level evaluations within the direct sweet-pepper/Capsicum evidence base report harvesting success rates of approximately 18–83% and source-reported cycle times of approximately 10–69 s per fruit under differing task boundaries, although direct ranking is inappropriate because environments, crop modifications, occlusion levels, sample sizes, task boundaries, denominators, and success criteria differ. As fruit detection and basic grasping improve, losses increasingly arise from incomplete action-ready information on maturity, pose, and peduncles; narrow approach and cutting tolerances; and weak recovery, unloading, and repositioning loops. Near-term development should investigate robot-friendly greenhouses, repeatable docking, local closed-loop control, and human-supervised or collaborative operation, while directly validating productivity, safety, workload, and economic effects. Medium-term priorities are active multimodal perception, fault-tolerant grasping and cutting, and coordinated mobile manipulation. Longer-term progress will depend on agronomy–equipment co-design and long-duration validation of reliability and economic viability.

candidates.title: Generative AI as a process of socio-technical co-evolution: a structured review of the transition from content generation to operational intelligence
candidates.abstract: In the era of the digital economy, generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has become a transformative force, and its impact extends far beyond the scope of content creation. GenAI has rapidly evolved from generating text, images, and code to assuming operational roles across industries, science, healthcare, and governance. Tracing this evolution requires more than a catalog of technical milestones. A dedicated analytical framework is therefore needed. This study constructs a comprehensive analytical framework organized around three intertwined axes: technology generation, operational intelligence, and socio-technical co-evolution. The framework is applied comparatively across five domains: industry, healthcare, education, finance, and public governance. Three cross-cutting principles emerge from this cross-domain analysis. These are situation-sensitive anchoring, dynamic trust calibration, and responsibility-aware delegation. Risk tolerance, cultural background, and the depth of domain-specific knowledge are identified as key moderators that shape the transition from generative tools to operational intelligence. By synthesizing evidence across these dimensions, this review identifies future directions for research, design, and governance of GenAI systems.

candidates.title: Responsible AI Guidelines Fall Short at Work? How Responsible AI governance can benefit from the world of work perspectives
candidates.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming part of everyday work and people management, with potentially far-reaching consequences for employees, organizations, and labour markets. Yet the regulation of workplace AI is still evolving, leaving organizations and policymakers uncertain about what “Responsible AI” (RAI) means in practice. Governments, professional bodies, and organizations have produced a growing number of RAI guidelines. But do these guidelines help equip organizations and policymakers to govern AI in the workplace? This paper examines 183 organizational RAI guidelines to understand how they address work and employment issues. Our analysis identifies the main themes emphasized across the guidelines and reveals that work- and labour-related concerns rarely occupy a central position. It also suggests that, despite their proliferation, RAI guidelines remain centred on largely stable and abstract principles, with limited evolution in their normative focus. When workplace issues are mentioned, they are usually framed indirectly, most often through concerns about discrimination and employee safety. RAI frameworks therefore rarely confront the workplace directly, even though employment is one of AI’s most immediate and consequential arenas. We argue that anchoring RAI governance in established governance mechanisms – including international labour standards and fundamental principles and rights at work – can help organizations and policymakers ensure that workplace AI addresses ethical concerns in the world of work and promotes decent work.

candidates.title: A Decision‐Support System for Prioritizing the Transformational Dynamics of Autonomous Trucks Deployment
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT The implementation of autonomous technologies in commercial freight transportation has advanced significantly, with pilot programs demonstrating technical viability on major interstate highways. However, existing studies on freight innovation predominantly focus on technology adoption and efficiency metrics, often neglecting the broader organizational consequences of automation in logistics. Thus, the integration of autonomous trucks represents more than labor substitution or marginal productivity improvement. It initiates reconfigurations of freight flow control, service contracting, and the distribution of operational authority. Accordingly, this study analyzes the transformational dynamics of autonomous trucking deployment within North Dakota State's freight systems using integrated fuzzy consensus building (FCB) and fuzzy cognitive mapping (FCM) techniques. Through the analysis of 25 experts, this study identifies 16 critical transformation factors and models their causal interdependencies and structural importance. Results demonstrate that tech firm logistics control, industry structure transformation, and tech firm market entry exhibit the highest centrality values. In contrast, the traditional trucking market share declines systematically in dynamic simulations. A scenario‐based sigmoid sensitivity analysis is performed to assess the robustness of the results. The findings suggest stakeholders should urgently implement strategic adjustments before market dynamics solidify around platform‐dominant structures.

candidates.title: Can artificial systems become conscious?—Recursive embodied closure as an integrative framework
candidates.abstract: Recent advances in artificial intelligence, connectomics, and computational neuroscience increasingly raise the question of whether artificial systems—or even pure computer simulations—could become conscious. Contemporary theories emphasize embodiment, predictive processing, homeostatic regulation, and continuous interaction between cognition, body, and environment rather than isolated computation. We propose recursive embodied closure as an integrative framework linking embodied, predictive, functionalist, and dynamical approaches to consciousness. Rather than replacing existing theories, the framework identifies a shared organizational principle: the continuous recursive coupling of cognition, bodily regulation, action, and environmental feedback. We argue that consciousness may, in principle, emerge in artificial systems, including computational simulations, for three reasons. First, consciousness may depend on recursively closed loops linking cognition, body, and environment, and such loops could also be realized in robotic, neuromorphic, or virtual embodiments. Second, evidence from comparative neuroscience, convergent evolution, neurotechnology, and philosophy of mind suggests that the mechanisms relevant for consciousness are largely substrate-independent and may therefore be implemented in both biological and artificial systems. Third, although unknown physical mechanisms cannot be excluded, there is currently no empirical evidence for biological processes that are uniquely necessary for consciousness. Taken together, these considerations support the view that consciousness is best understood as an emergent property of recursively embodied, environmentally embedded cognitive systems rather than of biological matter itself. If so, biological brains, artificial neural networks, neuromorphic hardware, and even virtual agents may constitute plausible candidates for future artificial consciousness.

candidates.title: Ethics and Technology of the Mimetic AI Professor
candidates.abstract: A mimetic AI professor reproduces a specific human professor’s pedagogical method. Within an academic domain, the vocabulary, conceptual framing, and interaction patterns defining the AI mirror those of the human professor it emulates. In this model, knowledge is represented as accurate replication of a subject-matter expert, as opposed to generic subject-matter expertise. This paper provides an ethical and technical foundation for mimetic AI pedagogy by addressing three questions. First, it defines the concept of the mimetic AI professor and outlines why it may provide learning enhancement. Next, it outlines potential instructional roles the AI could play. Then, core human dilemmas that mimetic systems provoke are analyzed, and design responses are proposed. Finally, the paper consolidates as an ethics framework for mimetic AI professors containing these categories of ethical analysis: Autonomy, Dignity, Privacy, Fairness, Equity, Social wellbeing, Explainability, Performance. The framework intends to be useful for professors, engineers, and universities designing their own mimetic AI tools in the education domain.

candidates.title: A Qualitative Case Study on the Implementation of an AI-Powered Gait Rehabilitation Robot Program for Students with Severe and Multiple Disabilities
candidates.abstract: This qualitative case study explored how an AI-powered gait rehabilitation robot program was implemented over one semester in a special school and how its participants experienced and made sense of it. The bounded case was the program itself; its participants comprised three students with severe and multiple disabilities, the teacher-researcher (a special education teacher), a collaborating physical therapist, and three guardians. Data were collected from multiple sources, including health-management records and assessment sheets, class documents and Individualized Education Program (IEP) team minutes, robot-recorded gait data, semi-structured surveys and interviews, participant-observation logs, and the researcher’s reflexive journal. The data were analyzed through iterative coding, pattern identification, and cross-source comparison, with attention to discrepant data, and trustworthiness was strengthened through triangulation, member checking, and peer debriefing. Three themes were identified. First, the program was implemented within a co-teaching model that connected the special education teacher and the physical therapist across the boundary of education and therapy, and it was organized as a related service through IEP team consultation under the 2022 revised special education curriculum. Second, the participants moved from initial expectation and concern toward a more nuanced appreciation of the program, while also raising practical concerns about safety, sensor limitations, and the burden of responsibility. Third, the students showed uneven but meaningful changes. Although gains on the ordinal functional indicators (MMT, BBS, FAC) were partial or limited to maintenance, clearer changes appeared in confidence, self-efficacy, and social participation. Rather than verifying effectiveness, this case illustrates the possibilities and conditions of school-based AI gait-robot education and points to the need for a sustainable policy and institutional support framework, including the placement of rehabilitation professionals within schools.

candidates.title: Robotic automation of Caenorhabditis elegans lifespan based on active vision
candidates.abstract: Abstract The lifespan assay in Caenorhabditis elegans is a highly repetitive and labor-intensive procedure that can lead to counting errors and delays in obtaining results. Technicians and researchers should devote their time to more intellectually demanding tasks rather than simply observing the movement of nematodes. Full automation remains a major challenge across many fields, and it is particularly beneficial in preclinical research such as lifespan assays. Developing new techniques and evaluating their efficiency is essential in order to enable the large-scale adoption of these new methods. Previous work has automated plate inspection using sequences of images of Petri dishes captured with cameras. However, integrating these computational systems into robotic platforms greatly increases the capacity for high-throughput analysis of the plates and raises new questions, such as whether these systems could affect experimental results. In this work, we present miniTower, a robotic platform for automated lifespan assays, and show that it does not alter lifespan results and, in addition, enables high-throughput automated analysis, including during holidays, without human supervision. The approach was evaluated using the low-motility strain unc-1 , in which movement detection is more challenging, making it a suitable model for validating lifespan assays.

candidates.title: A meta review of programming and robotics in schools
candidates.abstract: Abstract This meta‐review explores the nature and scope of evidence syntheses on programming and robotics in primary and secondary education. It aims to identify benefits, challenges, and directions for future research, as well as to appraise the quality of evidence syntheses being conducted. A systematic search was conducted in Web of Science, Scopus, EBSCOhost (all databases including ERIC), and with the OpenAlex platform. After screening, 49 relevant evidence syntheses published between 2012 and 2023 were identified, and the Quality of Evidence Synthesis Tool (QuEST) was used to assess methodological rigour. Systematic reviews dominate evidence syntheses in programming and robotics education, with a recent rise in meta‐analyses, and publications were spread across 37 journals indicating interdisciplinary interest. Authors are mainly from Europe and Asia, with mostly domestic collaborations, and the overall medium quality of syntheses points to a need for more robust methodological standards. While programming and robotics education offer benefits such as enhanced cognitive development and creativity, challenges persist including resource limitations, teacher training, and cognitive load. The review calls for high‐quality, internationally collaborative research on effective pedagogical practices, cognitive load management, and the integration of AI in education. Context and implications Rationale for this study: While programming and robotics are increasingly integrated into school curricula worldwide, the quality, focus, and methodological rigour of existing evidence syntheses remain uncertain. This study systematically evaluates these aspects to clarify the current state of knowledge in the field. Why the new findings matter: This review provides an overview of 49 evidence syntheses, highlighting both educational benefits and challenges, and pointing to a need for more robust, internationally collaborative, and methodologically sound systematic reviews. The review not only synthesises what is known about programming and robotics research in primary and secondary education, but indicates where key gaps remain, helping to direct future research towards meaningful questions. Implications for researchers, practitioners, and policymakers: For researchers, the findings are useful in identifying research gaps and highlighting the methodological improvements needed in future evidence syntheses. Practitioners and policymakers can use these findings to develop better teaching practices, give teachers clearer guidance and resources, and focus on teacher training to address practical challenges.

candidates.title: Secure routing in internet of things using software defined networking and chaos theory
candidates.abstract: Abstract Secure data transmission in the Internet of Things (IoT) is a necessity, and the current secure routing paradigms, including trust-based distributed protocols and traditional RPL-based extensions, are usually characterized by high control overhead and high latency in dynamic environments because they cannot adapt to the frequent topology changes. In order to overcome these drawbacks, this paper presents a new secure routing architecture that combines Software-Defined Networking (SDN) and chaos theory. The process is in two stages: topology control and secure routing. First, SDN controller makes use of node mobility patterns and predicted link stability to pre-compute resilient clusters, which substantially lowers network reconfiguration frequency. Second, a lightweight chaotic encryption algorithm is presented, based on a dynamic initial condition based on the data payload itself in order to provide confidentiality at a low cost in terms of computational resources. The simulation outcomes prove that the suggested approach is better than the state-of-the-art protocols, as it enhances energy efficiency by about 23.7% and the ratio of packet delivery by 5.3%, which justifies its applicability to resource-constrained and dynamic IoT networks.

candidates.title: How Is Farmer Cooperation Possible? Interaction, Identity, and Community Capacity in a Chinese Rural Community
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT How can cooperation emerge in communities where institutional enforcement is weak and social relations are fragmented? Drawing on a longitudinal case study of Village L in rural China (2017–2021), this paper develops a five‐stage process model that explains the endogenous emergence of cooperation. Moving beyond incentive‐ and institution‐centered accounts, the analysis shows how cooperation is dynamically generated through a sequence of interactional mechanisms: initiated by exemplary action, expanded through observational learning and symbolic reinforcement, deepened through deliberative coordination that activates a collective identity, and stabilized through ritualization into a cooperative cultural structure. The study demonstrates that farmers' agency is not a pregiven individual capacity but an emergent, relational outcome of interactional processes unfolding over time. By examining how interaction, identity formation, and cultural stabilization are linked in practice, this article treats cooperation as an emergent social accomplishment rather than a fixed equilibrium or a problem of institutional design. It develops a process‐based explanation of how community capacity and collective agency are gradually built in rural settings marked by weak institutions and fragmented social relations. In doing so, the study speaks to ongoing debates in rural sociology about how cooperation is generated and sustained in everyday social life.

candidates.title: A brief history of dissociation as an Agent of Deterioration
candidates.abstract: The 10 ‘Agents of Deterioration’ (sometimes referred to as the ‘Agents of Change’) represent a framework for understanding the main threats to museum artefacts and other types of heritage, allowing conservators to plan how best to protect heritage when exposed to one or more of these threats. Most of the agents are physical or chemical in nature, such as water, pests and pollutants—but the tenth agent, dissociation, is more of a theoretical construct. Dissociation can be considered a separation between an object and its related data or context, and may result in a situation where an object has become irretrievable within a complicated storage system, or cannot be identified because of a loss of its associated files, data or related parts. This article reviews the adoption of dissociation within the framework of the Agents of Deterioration, a reframing that positions dissociation as an axis of change affecting an object's value within a collection. This places it firmly within the remit of conservators—alongside that of other museum staff—in order to minimise the risks related to it. The article reiterates the way that conservators are not only concerned with the physical preservation of objects, but also the preservation of the intangible aspects of information and knowledge. Since the introduction of this agent, there has been further discussion about the nature of dissociation and the article will review some of the debates around expanding its definition to include the risk of objects becoming separated from wider cultural contexts and meanings, for example through a loss of connection with the originating community of the object. These areas of debate demonstrate the way that the agents can be used flexibly to address different needs, and offer a productive space to engage in wider museum debates, but always rooted in care for the object—the key remit of the conservator.

candidates.title: Toward brain-trained humanoid robots
candidates.abstract: A growing corpus of experimental research demonstrates that neuroimaging data can be leveraged to improve the performance of artificial intelligence models, including reinforcement learning models in robotics. However, most existing studies have focused on vision, audition, language, or reward and error signals recorded while the human brain acts as an observer. In this paper, we argue that humanoid robots, although not equivalent to humans, could offer a unique opportunity to use the neural signals associated with touch, or other embodiment-dependent neural signals. As a result, humanoid robots could significantly expand the range of brain regions and functional networks that could be targeted for brain-trained artificial intelligence, and open new horizons in terms of alignment and reasoning. We discuss the improvements that neuroimaging data could potentially unlock in the context of sensorimotor tasks, spatial navigation, sensorimotor integration, embodied alignment, embodied reasoning, and social integration, as well as the broader challenges and opportunities related to brain-trained humanoid robots.

candidates.title: Conservation-oriented comparison of non-contact robotic survey systems for immovable cultural heritage in constrained environments
candidates.abstract: Non-contact survey of immovable cultural heritage in complex and constrained environments faces challenges from limited accessibility, structural occlusion, GNSS denial, fragile materials, and strict deployment requirements. This review synthesizes evidence on aerial robots, ground mobile robots, special-purpose systems, including cable-driven robots and manipulators, and heterogeneous collaborative systems. Existing studies remain fragmented across individual platforms, algorithms, and application scenarios, limiting conservation-oriented cross-platform comparison. Through systematic literature screening, evidence-role classification, cross-platform coding, and technology-readiness assessment, platforms are evaluated in terms of conservation safety, task effectiveness, and deployment maturity. Results show that suitability depends on material sensitivity, spatial configuration, survey requirements, and deployment conditions. Current research emphasizes localization, path planning, and control, while giving less attention to embodiment and deployment design, despite their importance for accessibility, observation effectiveness, and field deployability. Accordingly, a design-first paradigm is proposed, integrating platform selection, embodiment design, low-disturbance deployment, and field validation for heritage-oriented robotics.

candidates.title: SSS–DDQN solution-space best-first search for robust trajectory tracking of Mecanum robots under partial observability
candidates.abstract: Robust trajectory tracking of Mecanum-wheel mobile robots under partial observability is challenging due to nonlinear motion coupling, noisy measurements, sensor dropout, and external disturbances. In this study, we propose an SSS*–DDQN solution-space best-first search controller for robust trajectory tracking of a four-Mecanum-wheel mobile robot. The proposed framework integrates extended Kalman filter (EKF)-based belief-state estimation, QMDP belief sampling, DDQN value evaluation, and SSS* OPEN-list search with LIVE/SOLVED node refinement. The EKF estimates the hidden robot state under noisy observations and dropout, the DDQN provides learned long-term value evaluation, and the SSS* search refines promising corrective-action clusters using beta-bound pruning, delayed MIN-sibling refinement, bounded OPEN-list management, and secondary lookahead. The controller is evaluated using lemniscate trajectory tracking and compared with EKF-belief PER-DDQN, QMDP-PER-DDQN, Alpha–Beta Minimax, and AB–DDQN Hybrid controllers. The proposed SSS*–DDQN achieved the best overall ranking with RMSE x y = 0.01906 m, MAE x y = 0.016074 m, and a cumulative reward of 1843.6. Compared with the AB–DDQN Hybrid baseline, it reduced RMSE x y by 12.93% and MAE x y by 17.80%. Statistical validation over multiple stochastic trials further showed the lowest mean RMSE x y of 0.01847 ± 0.00132 m and MAE x y of 0.01554 ± 0.00128 m, with narrow 95% confidence intervals. The results confirm that the proposed SSS*–DDQN improves robust action selection and provides consistent tracking performance under partial observability.

candidates.title: Large language models for social governance: An analytical framework and research agenda
candidates.abstract: Abstract As social governance becomes increasingly complex, traditional governance approaches face challenges such as information asymmetry, fragmented coordination, delayed risk response, and uneven public service delivery. Large language models (LLMs) offer new possibilities for knowledge processing, decision support, and human–machine interaction in this context. This article provides a comprehensive and framework-oriented review of research on LLMs, digital governance, public governance, and computational social science. It develops a governance-oriented analytical framework that links LLMs capabilities, governance functions, operating mechanisms, governance outcomes, and risk constraints. The review examines representative application scenarios, including emergency management, information propagation, intelligent rule of law, data governance, public security, healthcare, and e-government. The analysis highlights uneven evidence maturity across these scenarios: bounded tasks such as policy retrieval, public consultation, information summarization, and administrative document processing have clearer deployment pathways, whereas high-stakes simulation, legal reasoning, public security assessment, healthcare triage, and cross-departmental decision support require stronger validation and oversight. LLM-enabled social governance also remains constrained by hallucination, algorithmic bias, privacy leakage, weak explainability, resource inequality, accountability gaps, and institutional adaptation challenges. This article argues that LLMs should be understood as decision-support infrastructures embedded in accountable, auditable, and public value-oriented governance institutions.

candidates.title: Poisoning resilient federated learning for secure internet of medical things a systematic review
candidates.abstract: The current trend of the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) has facilitated intelligent healthcare, including real-time monitoring, remote diagnosis, and data-driven clinical decision support. This substantially increases the attack surfaces of medical cyber–physical systems. As a privacy-conserving paradigm, Federated Learning (FL) has been proposed to enable distributed IoMT devices to collaboratively train models without exchanging raw medical data. However, FL-based IoMT systems are highly susceptible to poisoning attacks, intrusion-based attacks, gradient leakage, and communication-level adversaries, especially in heterogeneous and resource-constrained setups. This paper presents a systematic and comprehensive review of poisoning-resilient FL for securing IoMT systems, which summarizes over 134 peer-reviewed articles published since 2020. Using PRISMA 2020 principles, we construct a unified, multidimensional taxonomy of data poisoning, model poisoning, backdoor attacks, Byzantine attacks, Sybil attacks, intrusion-based attacks, and communication-level attacks in medical FL deployments. In contrast to existing fragmented surveys, this work directly correlates attack types with cross-layer defense mechanisms, including robust aggregation, anomaly-based intrusion detection, differential privacy, cryptography, blockchain-enhanced FL, and lightweight hybrid strategies tailored for low-power IoMT devices. A comparative evaluation is conducted using real-world healthcare datasets, analyzing the trade-offs among detection accuracy, latency, communication overhead, computational cost, and energy efficiency. Finally, the research challenges and future research directions are identified to enable regulatory compliance, real-time clinical applications, and scalable edge-fog-cloud orchestration for next-generation secure IoMT systems.

candidates.title: Robot-assisted total laparoscopic pancreaticoduodenectomy with transvaginal specimen extraction: a case report
candidates.abstract: Natural orifice specimen extraction surgery reduces incision-related complications and accelerates postoperative recovery while maintaining oncologic safety, whereas the da Vinci robotic surgical system further enhances the precision of minimally invasive procedures. This case report describes a robot-assisted total laparoscopic pancreaticoduodenectomy combined with transvaginal specimen extraction (RPD-TVSE). The patient was a 64-year-old female with moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma of the descending duodenum. The procedure took 350 min, with intraoperative blood loss of 200 mL; no blood transfusion was administered during the perioperative period. The patient was able to ambulate on postoperative day 1, with no adverse events recorded. Histopathology confirmed tumor staging as pT2N0M0, with all surgical margins negative. At 12-month follow-up, no evidence of recurrence was observed. This case demonstrates that RPD-TVSE is technically feasible and yields favorable short-term outcomes, providing a novel minimally invasive surgical option for female patients. However, long-term oncologic safety requires further investigation and validation.

candidates.title: From “I created this” to “I love this”: How interactivity and output diversity shape continuance intention in GenAI-enabled product customization
candidates.abstract: Generative AI (GenAI) is increasingly embedded in product customization, yet little is known about how its affordances sustain user engagement beyond initial adoption. Drawing on Self-Determination Theory, this study examines how interactivity and output diversity relate to continuance intention through perceived design agency and customization satisfaction. Using an explanatory sequential mixed-methods design, we first surveyed 829 participants with recent GenAI experience after they completed a standardized exploration of a GenAI-enabled product customization platform, and then conducted semi-structured interviews with 13 participants to interpret the non-significant direct association between perceived design agency and continuance intention. Both affordances were positively associated with perceived design agency, customization satisfaction, and continuance intention. Perceived design agency, however, had no significant direct association with continuance intention; instead, the agency-continuance association followed an indirect-only mediation pattern through customization satisfaction. Interview findings further showed that felt authorship supported continued use when accompanied by a satisfying, feasible, and meaningful customization experience. These findings position perceived design agency as an upstream psychological mechanism rather than a direct driver of continuance intention and identify an affordance-agency-satisfaction pathway through which GenAI-enabled customization may support sustained use.

candidates.title: Mapping machine learning applications across the food value chain through a systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis
candidates.abstract: Abstract Food industry plays major role in public health, economic and environmental sustainability. Integration of machine learning (ML) is increasingly reshaping elements like safety protocols, quality management and supply chain optimization, though outcomes vary substantially by context and scale. This paper comprehensively synthesizes the ML applications by employing a systematic literature review (SLR) and a bibliometric analysis of 234 peer-reviewed articles published since 2014 and identifies prominent ML techniques like neural networks, support vector machines, and ensemble techniques. Various applications of these methods are food processing, fraud detection, personalized nutrition, and predictive maintenance. Collaborative pattern along with possible research directions are predicted using keywords co-occurrence and co-authorship network. Explainable AI (XAI), federated learning (FL) along with ethical rules are essential to ensure implementation and navigate AI driven revolution in food sector. Deep learning models have achieved very high classification accuracy in controlled food-quality trials, while early ML-driven dynamic-pricing pilots in SME grocery settings have reported substantial reductions in food waste and modest revenue gains; however, these results are context-specific and remain unconfirmed across broader, resource-constrained SME contexts.

candidates.title: LangBiTe: model-driven bias testing of text-to-text large language models
candidates.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have rapidly gained popularity across a wide range of applications, from customer support to content generation and decision support systems. However, LLMs have also been found to exhibit social biases, reflecting and amplifying stereotypes and prejudices present in their training data. Such biases can lead to harmful outcomes, particularly in sensitive domains. Addressing these risks is essential to ensure that the adoption of LLMs contributes positively to society without reinforcing existing inequalities. To facilitate a continuous, robust ethical assessment of text-to-text LLMs, we propose LangBiTe, a model-driven solution to configure and automate the testing of ethical biases. LangBiTe may uncover biases embedded within the LLM-based components of a software system and thus motivate adjustments, or the selection of a different LLM in line with the ethical requirements. The model-driven approach makes both the requirements specification and the test generation platform-independent and provides end-to-end traceability between the requirements and their assessment. Moreover, LangBiTe includes capabilities for an LLM-assisted generation of bias-testing datasets. We have implemented an open-source tool set, available on GitHub, to support the application of our approach. Finally, we present a series of case studies where LangBiTe was applied to unveil biases in several, popular online text-to-text LLMs, thus demonstrating the effectiveness of its diverse functionalities.

candidates.title: Record stack durability in industrial solid oxide steam electrolysis through operational control
candidates.abstract: Solid oxide steam electrolysis offers the highest electrical efficiency for hydrogen production, yet wide-scale deployment remains constrained by durability. Here, we show that long-term stack durability can be strongly influenced by operating strategy, achieving 25,000 h of steam electrolysis operation in a full 70-cell solid oxide electrolysis cell stack under frequency-dependent electrochemical operation (AC:DC). This experiment represents, to our knowledge, the longest and lowest degradation operation reported for a full stack. The stack enters a stabilized regime with an average voltage degradation rate of 0.05 % kh⁻¹ (0.65 mV kh⁻¹ per cell) sustained for 22,000 h after initial conditioning. The behavior is evaluated against initial DC operation, prior full-stack benchmarks, impedance evolution, and post-test microstructural signatures. Periodic polarity inversion between electrolysis and fuel-cell modes modulates electrochemical polarization and heat generation, consistent with mitigating thermal and electrochemical gradients that develop during sustained DC electrolysis. Stack-level impedance evolution and post-mortem microstructural analysis demonstrate stabilization of electrochemical performance and suppression of degradation signatures commonly observed under DC operation, indicating that key degradation pathways are not activated under AC:DC operation. By shifting durability control from materials to operational strategy, AC:DC operation offers a scalable pathway toward long-lived solid oxide electrolysis for economically competitive green hydrogen production. Demonstration of a long and low degradation solid oxide steam electrolysis experiment for a full SOEC stack, achieving 25,000 hours of operation through AC:DC operation showing potential for low-cost green hydrogen production.

candidates.title: Large language models as travel co-planners: the GIFT model of youth–AI interaction
candidates.abstract: This study examines how members of Generation Z and Generation Alpha perceive and use LLMs in tourism planning. Drawing on six age-specific focus groups with 57 participants (26 Generation Alpha pupils aged 11–14 and 31 Generation Z BSc students aged 20–24) conducted in Budapest, Hungary, the study uses a qualitative, Grounded Theory–informed approach to explore prior use, anticipated practices, credibility assessments, and the meanings attached to LLMs. Participants in both cohorts were familiar with digital technologies and valued fast, personalized services, but their accounts differed in decision-making autonomy, social embeddedness, and evaluative practices. Generation Alpha participants more often positioned LLMs as an exploratory assistant within family-based decision structures, whereas Generation Z participants more frequently described comparing or verifying AI-generated outputs through other sources and social input. These patterns are better understood as different modes of credibility assessment and reliance than as simple differences in trust. The resulting GIFT ( Generational Interpretations of Future-oriented Technologies ) framework conceptualizes youth–AI interaction in tourism planning as context-dependent, with LLMs serving as cognitive support tools and potential co-creators. GIFT is presented as an exploratory framework grounded in this sample rather than as a universal theory. The study links human–AI interaction to the social contexts in which young people make travel decisions and offers implications for tourism professionals, educators, and AI developers.

candidates.title: What If We Work Together? Fostering Reflections on Designer Inclusion in Open Source Software Through Speculative Design
candidates.abstract: Open source software (OSS) often prioritizes technical functionality over usability and UX design. This imbalance limits OSS adoption among broader, non-technical users. Key underlying factors contributing to this issue are the shortage of design expertise in OSS and a dominant developer-centric mindset. To address these persistent issues, we explore the potential of speculative design as a catalyst for transforming the OSS community’s mindset towards a more designer-inclusive environment. Our design was informed by an analysis of online forums, which revealed designers’ motivations and challenges when contributing to OSS. Guided by these insights, we created two speculative societies, Husia (collectivist) and Reetar (individualist), in which designers are valued for different reasons and their work incorporated in different ways. Through a user study with 12 OSS practitioners (seven designers and five developers), we found that our speculative societies provoked participants’ rich and critical reflections on OSS values, the root causes of challenges, and proposed actions. Our work provides insights into how speculative design can be used in the practical, sociotechnical context of OSS to stimulate critical reflection, improve awareness, and yield recommendations for fostering an equitable, sustainable, and inclusive OSS environment.

candidates.title: How can we measure AI-skill demand using online job advertisements? Comparing indicators using German labour market data
candidates.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) tools into work processes drives growing demand for AI-related skills. Researchers and policy makers need a reliable measure of regional AI-skill demand to understand and react to these changes. We discuss the advantages and disadvantages of indicators including absolute numbers, shares, and location and normalised location quotients. We compare regional indicators using 34 million online job advertisements from 2021 to 2024 allocated to German spatial planning regions (Raumordnungsregionen, ROR). We find that the normalised location quotient is the most reliable measure, capturing the nuances of AI-skill demand even in less densely populated regions.

candidates.title: The AI technological shock and sustainable development: a systemic analysis of entrepreneurial ecosystems
candidates.abstract: Abstract In a context of increasing global uncertainty and accelerating digital transformation, it is analysed how frontier technologies, such as artificial intelligence (AI) and robot density, constitute an external technological shock that influences and reshapes entrepreneurial ecosystems and sustainable development. To analyse this effect, the entrepreneurial ecosystem scheme developed by Galindo and Méndez [34], based on Parsons’s AGIL framework and incorporating external factors, is adopted, considering technological shock as the sole external factor. The empirical analysis is conducted using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) for a panel of 12 European economies over the period 2022–2024. The results reveal that the technological shock associated with AI has asymmetric effects across ecosystem dimensions, with strong and significant effects on economic and juridical factors, more moderate effects on the political dimension, and weaker effects on the cultural dimension. Furthermore, the findings show that technological shock contributes to stimulating both entrepreneurial activity and sustainable development. The study also highlights the key role of institutional quality and economies’ absorptive capacity in translating technological change into sustainable outcomes. By integrating a systemic sociological approach with entrepreneurial ecosystem theory, this research provides new evidence on how emerging technologies reshape the structural functioning of entrepreneurial ecosystems and this has import implications for policymakers seeking to align innovation, entrepreneurship, and sustainable development.

candidates.title: Conditions and Processes: Why and How Does Peer Production Work?
candidates.abstract: Dana Lewis is a health communications professional who, like millions around the world, lives with type 1 diabetes.Type 1 diabetes is a chronic medical condition that impedes the pancreas from producing insulin, which keeps blood glucose levels within a healthy range.People with type 1 diabetes constantly monitor their blood glucose levels, and then pump or consume insulin as needed.The glucose monitors on the market when Dana was diagnosed, however, only issued alerts that were not loud.A heavy sleeper, Dana worried that she might miss an alert in the middle of the night and wind up in the emergency room.Prompted by a conversation on modifying her glucose monitor on Twitter in 2013, Lewis worked with Scott Leibrand to calibrate her monitor so that it could predict changes in her blood sugar hours in advance. 1 She shared hardware specifications and software for her solution

candidates.title: LLM-Storyteller: child-guided narrative co-creation via real-time adaptive prompting and visualization with an embodied robot
candidates.abstract: Interactive storytelling has shown great potential in supporting children's creativity. However, existing robotic storytelling systems mostly treat the robot as the primary author or lack the ability to adapt to a child's interaction state in real time. In this paper, we present LLM-Storyteller, an embodied robotic system designed for child-guided narrative co-creation. The system preserves the child's authorship by acting solely as a facilitator through adaptive prompting, which adjusts based on real-time classification of the child's interaction state. Furthermore, it closes the creative loop by transforming the child's narrated story into a personalized animated cartoon. The architecture integrates local automatic speech recognition, state detection, an adaptive Large Language Model (LLM) prompt engine using Llama 3.2, and a story-to-animation pipeline utilizing Stable Diffusion XL. We evaluated the system across 12 simulated storytelling sessions, all of them role-played by the two authors rather than by children, measuring response latency, animation generation time, interaction state distribution, and the lexical origin of the narrative. Authorship was approximated by Lexical Narrative Ownership, the share of unique content words in the finished narrative that the simulated child introduced before the robot did. This share reached 0.87 on average, and 58 of 72 robot turns followed the measured question-based response format. Together, these indicate that the narrative vocabulary originated with the child, which is evidence of facilitation rather than a semantic proof of story ownership. An internal rating of the outputs by the two authors across four dimensions gave the highest scores to follow-up question quality and the lowest to image-story alignment. All findings are bounded to prototype-level feasibility under simulated conditions, since no children took part.

candidates.title: A latency-aware framework for visuomotor policy learning on industrial robots
candidates.abstract: Industrial robots are increasingly deployed in construction and manufacturing tasks, where the deployment of end-to-end visuomotor policies is challenged by the observation–execution gap induced by observation, inference, and execution latencies. This gap is often significant on industrial robotic arms due to high-level control interfaces and slower closed-loop dynamics, making execution timing a dominant system-level concern. This paper presents a system-level, latency-aware framework for deploying and evaluating visuomotor policies on industrial robotic arms. The framework integrates latency-calibrated multimodal sensing, data synchronization, a unified communication pipeline, and a teleoperation interface for collecting expert demonstrations. Within this framework, we formalize a latency-aware execution strategy that assigns timestamps to policy-predicted action sequences and schedules only temporally feasible actions according to their intended execution time, enabling asynchronous inference and execution without modifying policy architectures or training procedures. We evaluate the framework on a contact-rich assembly task while systematically varying inference latency and compare latency-aware execution against blocking and naive asynchronous baselines using identical policies and sensing modalities. Results show that latency-aware execution preserves smooth motion, compliant contact behavior, and task progression consistent with demonstrations across inference latencies of 100–500 ms. Latency-aware execution maintained task duration and motion smoothness within 13% and 9% of the demonstration reference, respectively, while avoiding the latency-dependent slowdown observed under blocking execution and the large contact-force overshoots produced by naive asynchronous execution. These findings demonstrate that explicit handling of the observation–execution gap is essential for reproducible, closed-loop deployment of visuomotor policies on industrial robotic platforms.

candidates.title: Reframing Home: Diasporic Hybridity, Spatial Aesthetics, and Affective Spectatorship in Arab-Canadian Cinema
candidates.abstract: This dissertation argues that Arab-Canadian cinema constitutes a politically significant cultural formation that actively shapes, rather than merely reflects, the diasporic identities of Arab and Muslim communities in Canada. Analysing fictional and documentary works produced between the early 1990s and the mid-2020s - such as Ruba Nadda's Sabah (2005) and Cairo Time (2009), Bachir Bensaddek's Montréal la blanche (2016), Pierre Sidaoui's A Scent of Mint (2002), Nisreen Baker's Things Arab Men Say (2016), and Arab Women Say What?! (2023) among others - the study contends that these films generate representational spaces in which identity is negotiated and reimagined against Orientalist misrepresentation, post-9/11 racialisation, and the structural asymmetries concealed within Canadian multicultural discourse. Three analytical frameworks structure the inquiry. The first draws on Bhabha's theory of hybridity and the third space, Brah's diaspora cartographies, and Anzaldúa's borderlands concept to examine diasporic identity as an embodied, processual negotiation expressed through spatial configurations, sensory aesthetics, and elemental metaphor. The second applies Crenshaw's intersectionality paradigm and critical race theory to analyse the interlocking operations of race, gender, religion, and class in the films' representations of Arab and Muslim femininity, masculine vulnerability, and the differential politics of mobility in Canadian urban space. The third builds on Hall's encoding/decoding model to investigate how filmmakers encode counter-narratives within institutionally legible genres, and how those narratives are decoded across the media ecologies that mediate their reception. The study concludes that Arab-Canadian cinema refuses equally the consolations of nostalgic return and the demands of assimilationist integration, developing instead a formal vocabulary - generic hybridity, archival poetics, testimonial intimacy - commensurate with the complexity of diasporic experience and constitutive of an enduring intervention in the politics of representation in multicultural Canada.

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence: Ethics in usability
candidates.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has profoundly changed and will continue to change our lives. AI is being applied in more and more fields and scenarios such as autonomous driving, medical care, media, finance, industrial robots, and internet services. The widespread application of AI and its deep integration with the economy and society have improved efficiency and produced benefits. At the same time, it will inevitably impact the existing social order and raise ethical concerns. Ethical issues, such as privacy leakage, discrimination, unemployment, and security risks, brought about by AI systems have caused great trouble to people. Therefore, AI ethics, which is a field related to the study of ethical issues in AI, has become not only an important research topic in academia, but also an important topic of common concern for individuals, organizations, countries, and society. This paper will give a comprehensive overview of this field by summarizing and analyzing the ethical risks and issues raised by AI, ethical guidelines and principles issued by different organizations, approaches for addressing ethical issues.
