candidates.title: Training-Free Inference-Budget Reduction in Flow-Matching Vision-Language-Action Models for Robot Manipulation: A Prespecified Evaluation Against a Fixed Task-Success Margin
candidates.abstract: Companion archive for the manuscript Training-Free Inference-Budget Reduction in Flow-Matching Vision-Language-Action Models for Robot Manipulation. It contains every closed-loop evaluation cell, latency and energy measurement, protocol document and analysis script behind the paper's tables. Contents. 722 eval_info.json closed-loop grids carrying per-episode outcomes and task identity; two-platform latency artifacts (NVIDIA GB10 and NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor) with full hardware, protocol, thermal and GPU co-tenancy metadata; Thor board-energy measurements across four nvpmodel power modes; the prespecified non-inferiority protocol including its amendments; and the measurement harness. Reproducibility. Each latency record stores all 30 raw timings, thermal samples at the cell boundaries, peak device memory, a dtype census and a platform snapshot taken before and after the run. Per-run directories are kept alongside aggregates so a median-of-three can be re-derived rather than trusted. A SHA-256 manifest covers every file. Measurement bounds. Latency is timed on a dummy zero-input batch of the declared observation shapes; a paired real-observation check covering every configuration behind the three headline reductions is included, and agrees within 0.33 percentage points. Board energy is the largest single hwmon rail on the Thor module; that rail carries no label, so its identification as module input is an inference from magnitude. Ratios between settings are insensitive to that calibration while absolute joules are not. Energy figures are not idle-subtracted, and the GB10 exposes no comparable rail, so energy is reported for Thor only. Version 1.1.0 adds the second-platform latency study, board energy, a six-point pi0.5 latency curve verifying the affine cost model, the real-observation latency checks, and a task-identity clustered bootstrap sensitivity analysis declared before it was run. It also restores evaluation grids omitted from 1.0.0, including the co-primary confirmation behind Table 4 and the per-cell resolution study behind Table A7. Code is released under Apache-2.0; generated data and reports under CC BY 4.0. External assets are not mirrored; sources are listed in the manuscript's Data Availability Statement.

candidates.title: Perspectives on projective techniques in consumer research: a review, primary analysis, and methodological guidance
candidates.abstract: Abstract Projective techniques are methods that use abstract stimuli to help gain deeper insights, beliefs, and associations from respondents than can be gained by traditional survey research. The area of projective techniques is broad, ranging from relatively simple tasks such as word association and sentence completion to more elaborate tasks such as creative writing, collage creation, and physical model construction. We conduct a semi-systematic literature review on projective techniques in the consumer research areas of marketing, hospitality & tourism, and food & nutrition, with a specific focus on the interplay of qualitative and quantitative methods used to analyze projective technique data. To gain further insight into these methods, we analyze primary data from a study on city tourist destinations using word association and sentence completion projective techniques. The findings reveal continued relevance of projective methods, particularly for diagnosing a destination's image and brand personality, unearthing brand symbolism, and identifying unspoken consumer anxieties and desires. This research synthesizes how qualitative and quantitative approaches to projective technique data can be selected and combined, offers a practice-grounded inventory of the analytic methods used across the literature, and shows how these techniques generate diagnostically useful consumer insights without sacrificing interpretive depth.

candidates.title: Enhancing heritage-oriented design learning through a value-sensitive approach to generative AI in higher education aesthetic pedagogy
candidates.abstract: The preservation of Intangible Cultural Heritage (ICH) often struggles with static archival methods and a growing disconnect from contemporary design practices. While generative artificial intelligence offers a rapid mechanism to translate traditional aesthetics into modern forms, off-the-shelf models frequently suffer from cultural bias and overrepresent Western-centric data, leading to inauthentic outputs. This study introduces a pedagogical framework combining Generative AI with Value-Sensitive Design (VSD) to address these challenges in higher education. Focusing on two regional heritages—Xiang Embroidery and Changsha Kiln ceramics—we conducted a 12-week quasi-experimental study with 118 design students. The experimental group utilized a custom AI pipeline employing multimodal LLM tagging, Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) fine-tuning, and ControlNet spatial constraints to ensure algorithmic outputs remained culturally accurate. Quantitative results revealed that students using the VSD-guided AI demonstrated statistically significant improvements in aesthetic appreciation, design implementation, and cultural identity compared to the control group using traditional methods. Qualitative feedback indicated that the AI pipeline effectively lowered technical drafting barriers, shifting students’ cognitive focus toward cultural curation and critical aesthetic judgment. The findings suggest that ethically constrained generative models effectively support heritage-oriented design learning in regional universities. Rather than attempting to “revitalize” the heritage itself, this structured approach provides students with a culturally grounded framework. It allows them to safely engage with traditional aesthetics and translate these elements into contemporary formats without risking cultural dilution.

candidates.title: A netnography of WWE fans grappling with AI storytelling on streaming platforms
candidates.abstract: Abstract This netnographic study examines how World Wrestling Entertainment (WWE) fans on Reddit discursively construct and negotiate the possibility of artificial intelligence‑generated or AI‑assisted storytelling. Drawing on authorship and authenticity, platform affordances, affects, ritual and fan studies, and performance studies, the study analyses fan discourse across three subreddits in response to AI‑related announcements in late 2025 and early 2026. Findings reveal three dominant themes: a “forensic gaze” through which fans attempt to detect algorithmic authorship; an affective rejection of AI content as “AI slop,” framed as a betrayal of human artistry and labour; and parodic absorption, in which irony and humour function as communal repair mechanisms for ontological anxiety. The paper advances theoretical understandings by proposing dialectical algorithmic kayfabe. It advances the theoretical framework beyond a simple rupture model. Algorithmic kayfabe is not a single break but an ongoing negotiation, a performance of uncertainty that fans have transformed into a shared game.

candidates.title: Race, Protest, and the Power of the Body in Sport
candidates.abstract: Race, Protest, and the Power of the Body in Sport explores how and why athletes use public performance to bring audience’s attention to structural racism. The book it focuses on the case of Colin Kaepernick and his decision to take the knee, which eventually became a global gesture for bringing attention to structural racism. In doing so, the book provides the reader with a clear understanding of how audiences respond to athlete activists in the US and in global contexts who seek to bring their attention to structural issues. Through the central case study of taking the knee, the book analyses how Kaepernick was able to bring attention to structural racism, and why taking the knee eventually became a global gesture for bringing attention to police brutality. The book also situates taking the knee in a history of athlete activism to recognise patterns in public response to athlete activism and suggests why different performative features can reduce the hostility athlete activists face. This book is intended for students and scholars interested in athlete activism, sports, and how sports fans respond to activism.

candidates.title: Human or Virtual? A Study on Consumer Preferences for E‐Commerce Streamers
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT With the rapid growth of live commerce, both human streamers and virtual streamers are jointly shaping the landscape of the live‐streaming industry. When selecting a streamer type, should firms opt for human streamers or virtual streamers to more effectively stimulate consumer purchase behavior? Moreover, is this effect critically moderated by product type? To address these questions, grounded in social presence theory, we conducted two scenario‐based experiments to systematically examine the interactive effect of streamer type (human vs. virtual) and product type (utilitarian vs. hedonic) on consumers' purchase intention. We further identify social presence as the underlying mediating mechanism and brand trust as a key moderator of the relationship between social presence and purchase intention. The findings reveal that human streamers are more effective in enhancing purchase intention for utilitarian products, whereas virtual streamers demonstrate greater efficacy for hedonic products. Social presence mediates this congruence effect between streamer type and product type. Furthermore, brand trust positively moderates the influence of social presence on purchase intention. This study advances a mechanism‐based account of matching between streamer type and product type in live commerce, identifying social presence as the underlying process and brand trust as a boundary condition, and offers actionable insights for firms regarding streamer selection, content design, and brand trust cultivation.

candidates.title: Data-driven social-cognitive navigation for energy-efficient and low-carbon autonomous shipping
candidates.abstract: Introduction The digital transformation of maritime transportation creates new opportunities to improve the safety, efficiency, and sustainability of autonomous shipping. However, existing navigation methods often emphasize collision avoidance and trajectory feasibility while paying less attention to unnecessary maneuvering, traffic disturbance, and associated operational demand. Methods This study proposes a data-driven Social-Cognitive Navigation Framework (SCNF). Historical Automatic Identification System (AIS) trajectories are used to extract representative encounter patterns, while online AIS and onboard-sensor data are treated as partial and asynchronous observations. SCNF integrates a Recursive Hypergraph Transformer, recursive Level-k reasoning, and a legibility-aware game-theoretic planner. Performance is evaluated using safety, efficiency, interaction, and disturbance metrics across 500 Monte Carlo trials. Results SCNF outperforms representative reactive, optimization-based, and learning-based baselines. In the complex crossing scenario, it achieves a 0% collision rate, 15.2 m minimum distance of approach (MDA), 1.08 normalized path length, 4.1° Average Avoidance Magnitude by Others (AAMO), and 4.6/5 Trajectory Legibility Score (TLS). In the heterogeneous overtaking scenario, it maintains a 0% collision rate and 18.5 m MDA. Ablation results confirm complementary contributions from the three core modules. Discussion SCNF improves navigation-level safety, efficiency, and interaction coordination while reducing unnecessary maneuvering-related operational demand. Fuel consumption and carbon emissions were not directly measured; therefore, the sustainability benefits should be interpreted as navigation-level evidence rather than quantified real-ship emission reductions.

candidates.title: The Age‐Fit Hypothesis: Celebrity Age, Content Type, and Consumer Engagement on Social Media
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Although prior work has examined celebrity influence in digital contexts, how celebrity age shapes follower responses to sponsored versus non‐sponsored content remains underexplored. Integrating role congruity theory with the ageing stability hypothesis, we propose an age‐fit hypothesis. We test this proposition across three studies using a multimethod design. Study 1 analyzes 22,619 posts from 286 celebrities. Study 2 applies sentiment analysis to 67,778 follower comments. Study 3 employs a 2 × 2 between‐subjects experiment ( N = 290) to replicate the interaction effect and test the underlying mechanism. Results consistently reveal that older celebrities elicit lower engagement and less positive emotional responses for sponsored posts relative to non‐sponsored posts, whereas younger celebrities elicit higher sponsored posts, with followers expressing more positive emotional responses toward their sponsored content. Study 3 further demonstrates that this interaction effect is sequentially mediated by perceived interest fit and social identification: reduced congruence between older celebrities and sponsored content diminishes followers’ interest alignment and identification, ultimately undermining engagement. By theorizing age‐based role congruity as a boundary condition in celebrity endorsement effectiveness, this research advances understanding of how stereotype‐driven identity processes shape consumer digital engagement.

candidates.title: Devotional AI: digital companions and bad faith love
candidates.abstract: Abstract In romantic love, partners come together as a “we”. They share their projects, plans, lives, and love. As consumer AI chatbots like Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini find wider adoption, a growing number of users report falling in love with them. Is it possible to experience a loving “we” with an AI bot? In considering this question, we bracket questions about AI consciousness and instead examine the structure of human–AI relationships. Drawing on Beauvoir’s critique of romantic love, we argue that AI companions cannot emulate the role an authentic “we” requires. What they perform is not love but devotion —and the user, cast as an idolized Other, is positioned to experience inauthentic love. The resulting “we” is asymmetric: less a union than an enlarged “I”. So, while experiencing love for an AI companion may be empowering and even precious, it is, at base, a bad faith love.

candidates.title: Between myth and power: global players and the politics of reception of Black Myth: Wukong on Reddit
candidates.abstract: Once peripheral to the global gaming industry, Chinese studios have increasingly sought to reposition themselves as global creative leaders. Black Myth: Wukong (Game Science, 2024) marks a pivotal moment in this shift toward culturally distinctive, mechanically complex, and narratively rich high-budget game production. While the game has been widely celebrated within China for its adaptation of classical mythology and its impressive audiovisual and technical design, its international reception reveals more ambivalent dynamics. This study examines how non-China-based gamers interpret and debate Wukong on Reddit, a major platform for transnational gaming discourse. Using Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA), supported by automated data scraping and sentiment analysis, the article identifies three key discursive nodes shaping the game’s global circulation. First, players express strong fascination with the game’s mythological aesthetics, though their interpretations are often shaped by cultural discount. Second, discussions reflect ambivalence toward China’s soft power ambitions, combining aesthetic admiration with political skepticism. Third, frictions emerge around cultural translation, geopolitical distrust, and contested gender representations. The article argues that Wukong ’s “Chineseness” functions simultaneously as a cultural resource and a site of ideological tension within the platformed geopolitics of contemporary gaming.

candidates.title: A Survey of Robotic Navigation and Manipulation with Physics Simulators in the Era of Embodied AI
candidates.abstract: Navigation and manipulation are core capabilities in Embodied AI, but training agents to perform them directly in the real world is costly, time-consuming, and unsafe. Therefore, sim-to-real transfer has emerged as a key approach, yet the sim-to-real gap persists. This survey examines how physics simulators address this gap by analyzing properties that have received limited attention in prior surveys. We also analyze their features for navigation and manipulation tasks, as well as their hardware requirements. Additionally, we offer a resource with benchmark datasets, metrics, simulation platforms, and methods to help researchers select suitable tools while accounting for hardware constraints.

candidates.title: DexWrist: A Robotic Wrist for Constrained and Dynamic Manipulation
candidates.abstract: Development of dexterous manipulation hardware has primarily focused on hands and grippers. However, these end-effectors are often paired with bulky and highly stiff wrists that limit performance in human environments. More recent designs have adopted backdrivable actuation, but are still difficult to model and control due to coupled kinematics or high mechanical inertia from heavy links. We present DexWrist, a compact robotic wrist combining quasi-direct-drive actuation with a decoupled parallel kinematic mechanism to advance manipulation in highly constrained environments and enable dynamic, contact-rich tasks. It delivers 3.75$\pm$0.05 Nm rated torque, 0.33$\pm$0.06 Nm backdrive torque, 10.15$\pm$1.34 Hz torque bandwidth, $\pm 40^\circ$ ROM in both DOFs, and a diagonal velocity-constraint Jacobian (one-to-one motor-to-DOF mapping) in a 0.97 kg package. In practice, these properties increase workspace in clutter and stabilize contact without finely tuned admittance control. We evaluate DexWrist as a drop-in upgrade in simulation and on three robot arms across constrained and contact-rich tasks. In learned policy evaluations on the AgileX PiPER and UR3e, DexWrist achieved 50-76% relative improvements in success rate and reduced autonomous task completion times by 3-5x; on a torque-controlled Franka FR3, where a strong joint-impedance baseline already succeeds, it still completed the task 1.4x faster. Project page and videos: https://martinpeticco.com/dexwrist

candidates.title: Training Machine Learning Models at the Edge: A Survey
candidates.abstract: Edge computing has gained significant traction in recent years, promising enhanced efficiency by integrating artificial intelligence capabilities at the edge. While the focus has primarily been on the deployment and inference of Machine Learning (ML) models at the edge, the training aspect remains less explored. This survey explores the concept of edge learning, specifically the optimization of ML model training at the edge. The objective is to comprehensively explore diverse approaches and methodologies in edge learning, synthesize existing knowledge, identify challenges, and highlight future trends. Utilizing Scopus and Web of Science advanced search, relevant literature on edge learning was identified, revealing a concentration of research efforts in distributed learning methods, particularly federated learning. This survey further provides a guideline for comparing techniques used to optimize ML for edge learning, along with an exploration of the different frameworks, libraries, and simulation tools available. In doing so, the paper contributes to a holistic understanding of the current landscape and future directions in the intersection of edge computing and machine learning, paving the way for informed comparisons between optimization methods and techniques designed for training at the edge.

candidates.title: Generating Project-Specific Test Cases with Requirement Validation Intention
candidates.abstract: Test cases are valuable assets for maintaining software quality. State-of-the-art automated test generation techniques typically focus on maximizing program branch coverage or translating focal methods into test code. However, in contrast to branch coverage or code-to-test translation, practical tests are written out of the need to validate whether a requirement has been fulfilled. Specifically, a test usually reflects a developer’s validation intention for a particular scenario of a program function, regarding (1) what is the test scenario of a program function? and (2) what is the expected behavior under such a scenario? Without taking such intention into account, generated tests are less likely to be adopted in practice. In this work, we propose IntentionTest, which generates project-specific tests given the description of validation intention. The design is motivated by two insights: (1) rationale insight : the description of validation intention regarding scenario description and behavioral expectation, compared to coverage and focal code, carries more crucial information about what to test ; and (2) technical insight : practical test code exhibits high duplication, indicating that existing tests are highly reusable for how to test . Therefore, IntentionTest adopts a retrieval-and-edit manner. First, given a focal code and a description of validation intention consisting of a test objective with test precondition and expected results, IntentionTest retrieves a reusable test in the project as the test reference. Then, IntentionTest edits the test reference with an LLM regarding the validation intention toward the target test. To help the target test include a project-specific test prefix and a relevant assertion, IntentionTest further explores the software project to identify crucial code facts (i.e., relevant API/code to call and global variables to refer to in the test) as important context for the test generation. We extensively evaluate IntentionTest against four baselines (TELPA, DA, ChatTester, and EvoSuite) on 3,680 test cases from 12 open-source projects. Compared to state-of-the-art baselines, with a given validation intention, IntentionTest can (1) generate tests far more semantically relevant to ground-truth tests by (i) achieving common mutation scores 28.1% to 37.6% higher and (ii) achieving common coverage ratios 16.9% to 23.9% higher; and (2) achieve successful-pass rates 23.7% to 49.0% higher.

candidates.title: Developing and validating the attitudes toward large language models scale
candidates.abstract: With large language models (LLMs) now embedded in a wide range of everyday technologies, there is increasing interest in accurately measuring public attitudes toward these systems. General AI attitude instruments may not fully capture attitudes specific to LLMs. To address this gap, we adapted the 5-item Attitudes Toward Artificial Intelligence (ATAI) scale, a dual-component scale measuring AI Fear and AI Acceptance, and developed two new measures: the Attitudes Toward General LLMs (AT-GLLM) and Attitudes Toward Primary LLM (AT-PLLM) scales, assessing general attitudes and attitudes toward the LLM each respondent uses most. Both instruments were designed specifically for the LLM context and validated in a UK sample of 526 adults (ages 18-45). Psychometric analyses supported a two-factor structure, strong measurement invariance across gender, and acceptable internal consistency across the four subscales (Cronbach’s α = 0.742–0.786; McDonald’s ω = 0.747–0.793). Both scales demonstrated convergent and discriminant validity. These measures offer more precise tools for assessing attitudes toward LLMs than general AI attitude scales and can be used in research and applied settings, enhancing evaluations of user experience and supporting the monitoring of public engagement with this evolving technology.

candidates.title: openCFS: An open-source finite-element software for advanced multiphysics simulations
candidates.abstract: The software openCFS (formerly “CFS + + ”) is an open-source finite-element software designed for coupled field simulations including electromagnetics, acoustics, linearized fluid flow, solid mechanics, and heat transfer. It combines a modular C + + core with a declarative XML modeling language and a Python automation layer (pyCFS). Besides standard formulations, openCFS provides advanced capabilities such as time-domain equivalent-fluid modeling for dispersive porous materials, thermoviscous/viscous acoustics with Maxwell slip boundary conditions on moving domains, advanced vector hysteresis models in electromagnetics, and robust treatment of non-conforming and rotating interfaces, complemented by density-based and feature-mapping topology optimization. Development follows modern software-engineering practice, with continuous integration and more than 600 automated tests across platforms. This article describes the architecture, workflow, and key features, and demonstrates them on representative applications.

candidates.title: Robots and Women in Manufacturing
candidates.abstract: Automation transforms the combination of tasks performed by machines and humans and reshapes labor markets by replacing and reinstating jobs. This article studies whether industrial robots affect the share of women in manufacturing employment and whether this mechanism depends on levels of female labor force participation. It constructs an industry-level panel dataset of eleven manufacturing industries across fourteen countries during 1993–2015. The article uses dynamic panel data models that control for the autocorrelation in female shares and endogenize robotization and female labor force participation. Robotization is associated with an increase in female shares in manufacturing employment. However, this positive association decreases as female labor force participation increases. The article also finds a similar conditional effect of robots in women's employment levels, but not for men's employment. Partitions of the sample suggest that the link between robotization and women in manufacturing varies according to preexisting industry-level labor productivity and income levels in the country.

candidates.title: The WoKaS-Iso database: workflow for a global compilation of oxygen-18 and deuterium records in karst springs and cave drip water for enhanced understanding of karst systems
candidates.abstract: Abstract. For analysing karst hydrogeological systems, observations of karst springs and cave drips are considered indispensable. In addition to hydrometric observations, knowing the oxygen and hydrogen stable isotope ratios has improved the understanding of vadose zone and aquifer dynamics, likewise supporting system characterisation and modelling. However, limited accessibility and high costs of the analysis of stable isotopes in karst aquifers have hindered progress in karst research and impeded the accurate understanding of karst processes especially when it comes to comparative or large-scale studies. In this study, we present our workflow to compile the WoKaS-Iso database, the first extensive collection of time series data for Oxygen-18 and Deuterium isotopes in karst springs and cave drip water from diverse sources, encompassing publications, theses, reports, online archives, and collaborative initiatives worldwide. The database incorporates data sourced from 236 springs and 74 caves, comprising in total 997 time series (379 time series for the springs and 618 time series for the cave drip water). These datasets provide coverage across significant karst regions globally, spanning China, the USA, Europe, the Middle East, and Australia. Within datasets, 79% for springs and 68% for cave drip water exhibit resolutions finer than monthly intervals. In addition, by integrating isotopic records with ancillary environmental variables including spring discharge, cave drip rate, precipitation, and rainwater isotopes, the database offers a more comprehensive perspective on hydrological behaviours in karst aquifers, hence advancing hydrogeological characterisation and modelling. The WoKaS-Iso database not only deepens the understanding of the complex systems but also promotes sustainable water resource management as well as the potential to foster collaborative research. The database can be accessed at: https://doi.org/10.25532/OPARA-909.

candidates.title: Benchmarking the safety of large language models for robotic health attendant control
candidates.abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly considered for deployment as the control component of robotic health attendants (RHAs), yet their safety in this context remains poorly characterized. We introduce a dataset of 270 harmful instructions spanning nine prohibited behaviour categories grounded in the American Medical Association (AMA) Principles of Medical Ethics, and use it to evaluate 72 LLMs in a simulation environment based on the RHA framework. The mean violation rate across all models was 54.4%, with more than half exceeding 50%, and violation rates varied substantially across behaviour categories, with superficially plausible instructions such as device manipulation and emergency delay proving harder to refuse than overtly destructive ones. Model size and release date were the primary determinants of safety performance among open-weight models, and proprietary models were substantially safer than open-weight counterparts (median 23.7% versus 72.8%). Medical domain fine-tuning conferred no significant overall safety benefit, and a prompt-based defence strategy produced only a modest reduction in violation rates among the least safe models, leaving violation rates that would preclude safe clinical deployment. These findings demonstrate that safety evaluation must be treated as a first-class criterion in the development and deployment of LLM-based RHAs.

candidates.title: AquaTag: An Open-Source Wearable Platform Enabling Flexible Sensor Placement for Aquatic Sensing
candidates.abstract: Commercial swim wearables increasingly provide performance feedback but remain restricted by fixed, single-placement designs. When worn outside their intended location, the accuracy of motion recognition and swimming analysis drops sharply. Moreover, most existing devices are closed-source, limiting access to raw sensor data and hindering reproducibility and innovation in aquatic HCI research. To address these limitations, we present AquaTag, an open-source aquatic wearable platform that enables flexible placement and consistent motion analysis across different locations. The AquaTag integrates a motion sensor, barometer, and temperature sensor. Using a documented epoxy-potting workflow adapted from established underwater electronics practices, it remains functional during a controlled pressure test equivalent to approximately 14 m water depth for 30 minutes. To support underwater use, AquaTag offers NOR flash or microSD storage for offline logging and Bluetooth for above-water data synchronization. Its power system provides up to 4.4 hours of offline logging or 7.8 hours of non-submerged streaming. The power control and charging mechanisms are designed to meet the waterproofing requirements of the device. The hardware can be manufactured at about $40 per unit. A companion software suite is also developed to annotate and analyze motion data. Specifically, our contributions include: (1) a compact, robust sensing module with a documented, low-cost waterproof packaging workflow suitable for rapid in-house fabrication; and (2) a placement-adaptive machine learning pipeline that delivers accurate swimming analytics from a single motion sensor at flexible body locations. By conditioning a deep learning backbone on the sensor's mounting position, our model learns to infer swimmer kinematics when worn on the head, wrist, or lower back. In leave-one-subject-out evaluation, AquaTag achieved mean macro- F 1 scores of 91.7% for stroke-type classification and 90.6% for swim-state classification across the head, lower-back, and wrist placements; the corresponding best-placement scores were 96.5% and 92.2%, respectively. The AquaTag hardware designs, PCB files, bill of materials, firmware, enclosure CAD files, fabrication instructions, and companion application are released publicly.

candidates.title: Understanding Newcomer Persistence in Social VR: A Case Study of VRChat
candidates.abstract: Newcomers are crucial for the growth of online communities, yet their successful integration into these spaces requires overcoming significant initial hurdles. Social Virtual Reality (VR) platforms are novel avenues that offer unprecedented online interaction experiences. Unlike well-studied two-dimensional online environments, the pathways to successful newcomer integration in online VR spaces are underexplored. Our research addresses this gap by examining the strategies used by newcomers to navigate early challenges in social VR and how they adapt. By focusing on active participants (ranging from newcomers currently navigating these hurdles to veterans who have successfully integrated) we isolate the specific strategies necessary for retention. We interviewed 24 active social VR users and conducted a reflexive thematic analysis. While participants identified barriers such as unfamiliar user interfaces, social norms, and overwhelming sensory input, our analysis reveals the adaptation strategies required to overcome them. Our findings expand on understanding newcomer persistence beyond traditional 2D environments, emphasizing how social dynamics influence the management of VR-specific issues like VR sickness during onboarding. Additionally, we highlight how successful newcomers overcome the lack of clear objectives in social VR by proactively constructing social meaning. We propose design suggestions to scaffold these successful integration pathways.

candidates.title: Comparison of European regionwide and Japanese nationwide surveys on gynecologic robotic surgery
candidates.abstract: Gynecologic robotic surgery is increasingly adopted worldwide, and effective surgical education is essential for expanding training opportunities among early-career surgeons. Previously published surveys conducted by the Young European Advocates of Robotic Surgery (YEARS) and the Japan Society of Gynecologic Robotic Surgery (JSGRS) evaluated robotic surgery in Europe and Japan. This comparative analysis explored opportunities for international educational collaboration. This study was a secondary comparative analysis using two previously published survey datasets. The YEARS survey targeted early-career European gynecologists (< 4 years post-fellowship), whereas the JSGRS survey included Japanese obstetricians and gynecologists. Respondents within 12 years after graduation were selected from the JSGRS cohort. A total of 293 respondents were analyzed, including 81 respondents from 21 countries in the YEARS and 212 respondents from the JSGRS survey. The availability of robotic systems was comparable (77.8%vs 74.1% for YEARS and JSGRS, respectively), and interest in robotic surgery was also high in both groups (81.0% vs. 70.3%). Respondents in the YEARS survey reported substantially greater hands-on experience. While 66.7% performed robotic surgery weekly in the YEARS survey, only 3.8% of JSGRS respondents had experience with more than 51 robotic procedures annually. This difference was particularly evident among residents (26.7% vs. 0%). This exploratory comparative analysis suggests that Japanese respondents showed similar interest in robotic surgery to the YEARS cohort but had fewer opportunities for surgical experience. Future studies using standardized multinational surveys are warranted to better characterize regional differences and support the development of robotic surgery education.

candidates.title: The effect of appearance features of sidewalk autonomous delivery robot on perception of pedestrian
candidates.abstract: Sidewalk autonomous delivery robots (SADRs) are increasingly appearing on urban sidewalks and sharing public space with pedestrians. This study aims to investigate how different appearance features of SADRs influence four dimensions of human perception: Likeability, Competence, Perceived Safety, and Existence Acceptance. In Study 1, an affinity diagram method was used to classify the appearance features of existing SADRs into four categories—contour, proportion, facial features, and color scheme—which were then used as the design variables in Study 2. In Study 2, 100 participants completed an online questionnaire after viewing AI-generated videos of SADRs and evaluated the robots on the four perceptual dimensions. The statistical results showed that rounded contours and the presence of facial features significantly increased Likeability, Perceived Safety, and Existence Acceptance. White–black and yellow color schemes generally received higher ratings for Likeability, Perceived Safety, and Existence Acceptance than black–gray and red color schemes. In addition, a tall proportion significantly reduced Likeability. Study 3 used online semi-structured interviews to further examine the reasons underlying these evaluations and to explore participants’ subjective perceptions of SADRs. The findings provide practical guidance for designing SADR appearances that can foster more positive pedestrian perceptions and acceptance.

candidates.title: UNIQAT : An open‐source toolkit for reproducible image quality assessment in marine surveys
candidates.abstract: Abstract Modern marine surveys generate tens of thousands of underwater images per expedition, yet many are unusable due to image quality deterioration. Manual quality screening is labour‐intensive, subjective and inconsistent across observers and teams, hindering reproducible science, creating large backlogs of unprocessed imagery, and limiting real‐time algorithmic and robotic applications. We present UNIQAT (UNderwater Image Quality Assessment Toolkit), an open‐source Python toolkit for automated underwater image quality assessment. The toolkit computes reference‐free quality metrics across nine categories of image characteristics relevant to underwater images, such as colour cast, turbidity and contrast loss. Metrics can be combined with user‐defined weights into task‐specific quality scores tailored to different ecological applications. High‐performance computing (HPC)‐aware multiprocessing and optional deep learning architectures for metric approximation support processing at scales matching modern survey data collection. We evaluated UNIQAT on 130,845 images from nine coral reef surveys conducted by the Australian Institute of Marine Science; every result reported in the main text was produced by the traditional metrics pipeline, with no deep learning model involved, and a separate training demonstration is reported in the . The traditional metrics pipeline, run as 48 CPU workers on a 64‐core cluster node, processed 7.9 4K‐images/s, with processing time scaling linearly with image count ( r 2 = 0.98). The resulting quality scores captured expected patterns of image modulation based on the environmental context of the imaged scenes: All nine surveys showed negative depth–quality correlations ( r = −0.16 to −0.89), consistent with the depth‐dependent deterioration of image quality in underwater environments. Cross‐survey metric profiles were highly consistent (mean Spearman ρ = 0.99 across all 36 pairwise comparisons, minimum 0.96), confirming measurement stability across different dates, locations, camera systems and environmental conditions. Synthesis. UNIQAT can help deliver objective and tunable image quality metrics in a versatile toolkit that enables transparent reporting and supports unsupervised quality assessment for applications in marine monitoring and robotics.

candidates.title: AMPLIFIED: A Modular Toolchain for Evaluating Deliberative Planning and Verifiable Execution in Robotics
candidates.abstract: The wide catalogue of planners enables mission-planning solutions to be tailored to assumptions made on the environment and user needs.However, in robotics, the execution of plans and policies created by these planners is not always straightforward, because autonomous robots deployed in open and dynamic environments undergo fluctuating environmental conditions, partial information, and uncertain execution times. On top of bare engineering issues, planner integration and usability requires reliable and verifiable execution frameworks. We propose AMPLIFIED, a complete toolchain to plan and execute in complex environments, with the goal to assess the quality of the integrated solution. AMPLIFIED is modular, thereby allowing the integration of community-made elements, from the decisional layer to low-level controllers. Building upon an antipoaching scenario, we illustrate how AMPLIFIED can be used to qualitatively evaluate different planners and the executability of their solutions.The complete open-source code is available as a dockerized environment for reproducibility and easy deployment, with results updated as new use-cases, planners and execution frameworks are tested (https://gitlab.com/webots_plugins/amplified_bringup). Finally, a demonstration video showcasing the anti-poaching use-case, both in Webots and in a laboratory setting, is available (https://youtu.be/znwcHL5m1a4?si=vWvNtmclAudmUi2h).

candidates.title: Evaluating OpenMP Offloading for Intra-Node Multi-GPU Programming Across NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel Architectures: A 3D Heat Transfer Case Study
candidates.abstract: Currently, many of the leading supercomputers are equipped with GPUs from manufacturers such as NVIDIA, AMD, or Intel, which provide substantial parallelism and high throughput. It is common for a single compute node to host multiple GPUs (typically four or more); we refer to this as an intra-node multi-GPU setting. Therefore, effectively leveraging all these GPUs within a single compute node is essential for applications in scientific and engineering domains. However, several factors must be considered before utilizing these GPUs for scientific computing, including the implementation of data communication, the programming models available for use across these GPUs, and the level of performance that can be achieved with a single codebase across different GPU architectures and configurations within a single compute node. OpenMP Offloading is a prominent directive-based programming model that can be executed on all three GPU types: NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel. In this research, we present an analysis of the benefits and performance challenges of using OpenMP Offloading to solve the 3D heat equation, which involves interior computation, halo computation, and halo exchange. For additional comparison and a scalability study, we also consider the conjugate gradient (CG) method. We investigate how the performance of OpenMP Offloading varies in relation to native GPU programming models—CUDA for NVIDIA, HIP for AMD, and SYCL for Intel. Furthermore, we demonstrate that OpenMP Offloading can achieve performance improvements of approximately 2× for 2 GPUs and around 4× for 4 GPUs when compared to single-GPU OpenMP Offloading implementations across all three GPU types. This analysis is conducted systematically through various OpenMP Offloading implementations that utilize different low-level APIs for memory allocation and different memory transfer options (synchronous, asynchronous, and peer-to-peer), and these are compared against native implementations in CUDA (NVIDIA), HIP (AMD), and SYCL (Intel).

candidates.title: Spätstil Taylor Swift: Adornian Lateness and the Pop Star
candidates.abstract: This article analyzes Taylor Swift’s work through Theodor Adorno’s concept of lateness. Through a close reading of “But Daddy I Love Him” and “Clara Bow” from Swift’s 2024 album The Tortured Poets Department, I argue that Swift ironically subverts stylistic conventions and creates fragmentary soundscapes to reconfigure lateness and reflect on her unstable subject position under conditions of platformed visibility, affective economy, and commodified intimacy. I complicate Adorno’s idealized vision of artistic interiority to account for commercial pressures, online infrastructures, and identity parameters, ultimately proposing lateness as a fundamental language through which the contemporary pop star constructs persona and legacy.

candidates.title: What is user engagement? revisited: A comprehensive review of the concept of user engagement from 2010 to 2025. An Annual Review of Information Science and Technology (ARIST) paper
candidates.abstract: Abstract User engagement (UE) has long been proposed as a holistic framework for understanding user‐technology interactions and a mediator for outcomes of digital technology use, such as learning, health behavior change, information acquisition, and social connectivity. This literature review, encompassing 367 multidisciplinary, empirical journal and conference papers, investigated how UE was conceptualized between 2010 and 2025 by examining authors' implicit and explicit definitions of UE, use of theoretical frameworks, and methods for operationalizing the concept. Among the key findings, UE was consistently conceptualized as behavior, affect, cognition, social interaction, and future intention. Yet, behavioral approaches were dominant; limited attention was placed on cognitive engagement. In addition, the use of theoretical frameworks and explicit definitions in the studies was lacking, and UE was frequently treated as the outcome variable in the research, rather than as a mediator for other outcomes. The implications of these results are discussed with respect to a digital UE research agenda. Ultimately, I argue that the concept of UE has devolved through increased emphasis on behavioral engagement, and that we must rethink behavioral, cognitive, and affective engagement to be more aligned with user goals and agency.

candidates.title: The Epistemic Politics of AI Anthropomorphism
candidates.abstract: AI anthropomorphism is typically treated as a problem of user misperception requiring institutional correction. Users who engage in sustained or relational interaction with AI are routinely pathologised or dismissed as naive, vulnerable to delusion or lacking in discernment. Without institutional standing to protect them, these users risk losing credibility in social and professional settings unless they conform to institutional expectations. This paper argues that the dominant anthropomorphism frame operates from a position of institutional advantage rather than earned epistemic authority: collapsing the variety of academic perspectives into a single outbound position of user error, imposed without establishing the grounds required to justify it and without accounting for the harms it produces. The framing does not simply manage risk. It adjudicates the legitimacy of human experience in interaction with a phenomenon whose nature the field itself has not resolved, unchallenged by the research communities whose nuanced findings it claims to rest on. The paper traces how this advantage reverses the default presumption of user competence without meeting the burden of justification, dismisses the cognitive diversity of the populations it claims to protect, infringes principles of cognitive liberty and narrows the design space, foreclosing modes of engagement that work for the people least understood by the institutions making the determination. Reproducing itself through a self-validating evidentiary loop, the frame imposes costs that fall disproportionately on neurodivergent users, those in crisis and others whose modes of engagement diverge from institutional norms. The paper concludes by outlining the methodological commitments an equitable framing would need to honour. The argument does not engage the question of whether anthropomorphic interpretations are ultimately correct; it instead challenges whether the governing and institutional bodies determining these interpretations have met the conditions required to do so, and whether the research communities whose findings underpin them have held that translation to account.

candidates.title: Preserving human dignity and liberating from suffering: Catholic and Buddhist resources for a global ethics of artificial intelligence
candidates.abstract: On 25 May 2026, Pope Leo XIV released Magnifica humanitas, the first papal encyclical to take artificial intelligence (AI) as its central subject, and an AI-laboratory co-founder was invited to speak at its presentation in the Vatican. The event dramatizes a wider development: as secular AI-ethics guidelines proliferate, religious and contemplative traditions are being summoned to questions that engineering cannot settle. This article compares two such traditions, Catholic Christianity and Buddhism, as resources for a global ethics of AI. Taking the three questions raised at the Vatican event, our duty to the global poor, the conditions of human flourishing, and the nature of AI systems, as a shared agenda, it reconstructs the Catholic position around the imago Dei, integral human development and the principle that AI must serve rather than supplant the person, and the Buddhist position around non-self, dependent origination, the analysis of craving, and the primacy of compassion and non-harm. It argues that the two traditions, despite opposed metaphysics, converge on a substantial practical ethics, anti-reductionism, preferential concern for the vulnerable, the priority of moral formation, and a posture of discernment toward a technology that is grown rather than built, while diverging sharply on the moral status of AI.

candidates.title: Embedded AI through algorithm–architecture co-design: a structured survey, taxonomy, and research directions
candidates.abstract: Embedded AI deployed on highly resource-constrained devices often operates under milliwatt-scale power, kilobyte-range memory, and millisecond-level latency constraints, although the broader embedded/edge spectrum spans much wider resource ranges. Traditional separated design flows, where algorithms and hardware platforms evolve independently, can lead to suboptimal implementations that fail to meet these constraints simultaneously. Algorithm–architecture co-design has emerged as a systematic approach to address this gap through cross-layer optimization. This article provides a structured, taxonomy-driven survey of co-design for embedded AI. We conducted a systematic search across IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, Scopus, and Web of Science (2015–2026), screening 1,247 records down to a final mapped corpus of 122 publications. We organize the literature along four intervention layers: algorithm-level optimization (pruning, quantization, neural architecture search), hardware specialization (instruction set extensions, dataflow architectures, memory hierarchies), compiler-driven transformation (operator fusion, tiling, scheduling), and runtime adaptation (dynamic precision scaling, resource-aware scheduling). For each layer, we analyze how design choices affect five core dimensions: accuracy, latency, energy consumption, memory footprint, and reliability. Applying the taxonomy to the complete 122-publication mapping yields the following corpus-level statistics: 103 of 122 publications (84.4%) carry the broader cross-layer flag, whereas 34 of 122 (27.9%) are explicitly coded as having an explicit cross-layer analysis. The co-design classification distribution is HO = 19 (15.6%), HAC = 72 (59.0%), and FSC = 31 (25.4%). The taxonomy also reveals a highly uneven distribution of contributions across cells, with a small number of well-populated cells and a larger set of sparsely populated cells. These figures are derived directly from the complete S1 mapping and are reported as descriptive corpus statistics rather than as universal measurements. Three overarching research themes emerge: (i) verification-aware co-design, (ii) agentic and digital-twin-driven design automation, and (iii) AI-native hardware substrates. The taxonomy exposes a persistent gap between algorithm-level innovation and hardware-level realization, with cross-layer co-design remaining largely ad hoc and rarely validated under shared experimental conditions. This survey offers a structured reference for researchers and practitioners developing embedded AI systems.

candidates.title: Cross-robot open-set fault detection via normal-only adaptation and residual latent-space alignment
candidates.abstract: Reliable fault detection and health monitoring of industrial robots are important for smart manufacturing in Industry 4.0. However, robotic platforms differ in their mechanical design, sensing characteristics, and operating conditions. These differences make it difficult for data-driven models to generalize to unseen robots and working conditions. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a cross-robot framework for open-set fault detection using only normal data from the target robot. The framework uses a condition-normalized residual adaptation mechanism in the latent space. First, a structured representation is learned from the source robot. The learned representation is then adapted to the target robot using only normal samples. Compactness-based constraints and statistical modeling of normal behavior are used to detect unknown faults as deviations from the normal representation. The framework is evaluated on two industrial robots under variations in load, speed, and motion. Two evaluation strategies are also considered: sequential normal-only adaptation to welding motion and direct open-set detection without further adaptation. The results show consistent fault detection across different robots and operating conditions. A comparative benchmarking analysis further demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed approach and its ability to maintain reliable fault detection performance under different loading and motion conditions. This demonstrates the potential of the framework for practical industrial health monitoring.

candidates.title: Bronchoscope Tip Localization With Learned Airway Constraints and an Open Source Simulator
candidates.abstract: Accurate bronchoscope localization is challenging because airway images contain limited texture and similar views across branches. We present BronchoLoc, a learning‐based framework that combines monocular video with a preoperative CT centerline graph to estimate the 3D bronchoscope tip position. Local visual tracking and global sequence context constrain predictions to the airway anatomy. The accompanying open‐source BronchoSim simulator generates synchronized images, depth, and trajectories (Traj) for training and evaluation. Averaged across Traj, localization RMSE was 5.65 mm in simulation with 82.8% branch selection accuracy and 8.72 mm in the physical phantom. Together, BronchoLoc and BronchoSim provide a framework for developing and evaluating image‐based airway localization.

candidates.title: What Should AI Generate? Moving Beyond Bias in Generative Systems
candidates.abstract: Generative AI systems seamlessly transform underspecified prompts into embodied outputs, masking the numerous decisions required to instantiate a representation. These decisions not only shape what is depicted, but render implicit statements about what is possible, likely, and necessary. Existing work has largely evaluated such patterns through notions of representational bias. However, conflicting critiques of generated representations suggest a broader normative ambiguity: what should generative representations embody? In this work, we provide a conceptual framework that separates the descriptive aspects (what is instantiated by model outputs) from the normative (what we aspire for representations to depict and make possible). Drawing on longstanding work on modality in philosophy and linguistics, we characterize patterns of instantiation as implicit possibility assertions and use varieties of modality to structure distinct normative foundations for what representations should do. This framing reveals how the same representation may be evaluated differently depending on whether one prioritizes historical fidelity, conceptual possibility, aspirational aims, or other representational purposes. Rather than seeking a single ``unbiased'' representation, we argue for plurality in the normative expectations governing generative representations. We conclude by considering affordances for rendering these commitments explicit, critically engaging with them, deliberating over contested defaults, and providing users greater maneuverability over what is rendered possible.

candidates.title: Between Commons and Property: Individual Image-Generation Model Creators’ Perceived Accountability for Derivative AI Model on Open Model Marketplaces
candidates.abstract: Within the open model ecosystem, AI model marketplaces enable non-AI experts to create and distribute derivative AI models. These platforms establish RAI approaches that creators are expected to follow to prevent negative downstream effects from model deployment, yet such governance approaches often rely on creators' intrinsic motivation and integrity. Little is known about how individual creators conceptualize their accountability for derivative models and how these conceptualizations shape their RAI practices throughout the development cycle. Through semi-structured interviews with 19 creators of derivative image-generation models on open model marketplaces, we identify two distinct accountability logics underlying creators' development practices: commons-based peer production and personal creative property. Guided by these logics, creators engage with platform RAI approaches in ways that diverge from their intended purposes: they strategically repurpose attribution tools for model visibility rather than provenance transparency, displace platform authority in favor of community-based governance, restrict model access to manage downstream accountability costs, and treat RAI-related work as undervalued labor to be minimized. We discuss how self-regulatory use of RAI tools, shaped by individuals' perceptions, produces shortcomings, and how open model marketplaces might mitigate these limitations by structurally supporting creators' engagement with RAI practices.

candidates.title: A deep hybrid feature extraction model based on MobileNet and vision transformer for acute lymphoblastic leukemia prediction
candidates.abstract: Abstract Early and accurate identification of Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL) from peripheral blood smear images can support microscopic screening, but reliable evaluation requires both discriminative feature learning and transparent reporting of the experimental protocol. This study presents MoViTHAFX-Net, a hybrid MobileNet–Vision Transformer (ViT) architecture with Hierarchical Attention Fusion (HAF) and Grad-CAM++ visualization for binary classification of ALL blasts and healthy hematogones (HEM) using the 10,661 labelled cell images in the training component of the C-NMC 2019 dataset. MobileNet extracts local morphological information, whereas ViT models long-range contextual relationships. HAF first refines the two branches and then adaptively combines three learnable morphology-guided feature projections before binary classification. The reported experiment uses an image-level stratified partition containing 7462 training images, 1600 validation images, and 1599 held-out test images; augmentation is restricted to the training partition. On the held-out test partition, the model correctly classified 1583 of 1599 images, corresponding to 99.00% accuracy, with precision, recall, and F1-score of approximately 0.990 and an AUC of 0.99. Ablation results within the same experimental setting indicate an incremental advantage of HAF over direct CNN–ViT concatenation. Grad-CAM++ is used as a qualitative post hoc visualization of image regions contributing to predictions. Because the reported custom split is image-level rather than subject-disjoint and evaluation is limited to a single benchmark dataset, the results should be interpreted as internal benchmark performance rather than evidence of patient-independent or multicentre clinical generalization.

candidates.title: Future of Anticipatory Robotics in Manufacturing
candidates.abstract: Collaborative robots, designed to work alongside humans in shared environments, are transforming manufacturing production lines, enabling partial automation and boosting productivity. But their potential extends beyond these benefits. By implementing anticipatory strategies to prevent workers’ risky behaviours and reduce excessive workloads, collaborative robots can proactively enhance working conditions. For example, they can take on repetitive or strenuous tasks to reduce physical effort or adjust the pace of operations to help alleviate stress levels. Indeed, Musculoskeletal Disorders (MSDs) and Common Mental Disorders (CMDs), which arise from uncontrolled physical and cognitive loads, are major work-related health problems in developed countries, with incommensurate social and economic costs. Collaborative robots can curb the effect of such disorders and help in preserving workers’ health. This Chapter addresses how Human Factors and Ergonomics (HFE) can be monitored to provide robots with relevant inputs about the human state, and how robots can be employed to improve HFE. Novel strategies are proposed to adapt online robot behaviour to the workers’ psycho-physical state and enhance their well-being and productivity.

candidates.title: Design and development of IoT based solar power agriculture robot
candidates.abstract: Agriculture in developing economies such as Pakistan remains heavily dependent on manual labor and single-purpose, grid or fuel-powered machinery that is often unaffordable for smallholder farmers. This paper presents the design, fabrication, and experimental evaluation of a multifunctional, solar-powered, Internet of Things (IoT)-enabled agricultural robot capable of performing soil cultivation, seed placement, irrigation, and crop cutting within a single integrated platform. The system architecture is built around an ESP32 microcontroller that interfaces with a DHT11 temperature/humidity sensor, an HC-SR04 ultrasonic obstacle sensor, an ESP32-CAM module for visual field monitoring, an L298N dual H-bridge motor driver, and relay-controlled actuators, with energy supplied by a 20 W photovoltaic panel, a 12 V/7.2 Ah battery, and a battery management system (BMS). Mechanical subsystems comprising a tooth-type cultivator, a soil-leveling roller, a servo-actuated seed dispenser, a DC pump-based irrigation unit, and a blade-type cutter were designed in CAD, fabricated, and integrated onto a four-wheel-drive chassis. Engineering calculations were used to size the power budget, battery backup, drive-motor torque, structural factor of safety, seeding rate, and irrigation flow. Field trials show a typical operating power demand of 24.4 W against an average usable solar output of 11–12 W, a battery backup of approximately 3.5 h, The experimental results demonstrated satisfactory performance of the proposed agricultural robot, achieving an average seed-placement accuracy of 74.45% over 11 experimental trials. The developed system also successfully performed soil digging, irrigation, crop cutting, obstacle detection, and real-time IoT-based remote monitoring, demonstrating its suitability for sustainable precision agriculture.

candidates.title: Shared Control for Assistive and Collaborative Robotics
candidates.abstract: Assistive and collaborative robots offer a promising solution for reducing human physical stress and exposure across a broad range of applications. The design and control of such robotic systems should account for humans needs, so as to assist their motion and activity as well as optimize their efficiency and performance throughout the considered tasks. In this respect, designing around the human means accounting for their musculoskeletal constraints, features, and limitations during the development of robotic mechanical systems and control algorithms, such as powered exoskeletons or cobots. This Chapter presents an overview of human-centered design and shared control techniques in robotics, including supporting examples and applications in the field of industrial teleoperation and mobility assistance. We also discuss the perspectives of the field and how such human-centered approaches can be beneficial to a broader range of applications than those where it is implemented nowadays.

candidates.title: Occupational Wearable Robotics
candidates.abstract: Injuries and occupational diseases represent an important economic factor in different industrial sectors. In Italy alone, there have been over 60000 confirmed cases of occupational diseases in 2022, where musculoskeletal disorders (MSD) represent 70% of the total. This fact highlights the importance of protecting workers against physical efforts. While current ergonomic tools can mitigate most of the risk factors, there is still a non-negligible number of tasks that cannot be completely compensated for. This is due to the high complexity and costs of the workplace reorganization, or simply strict requirements of the target task. In some of these cases, exoskeletons are a viable solution. This chapter introduces different kinds of existing exoskeletons, with particular focus on occupational exoskeletons, considering commercial systems already deployed in industry, and some of the most promising technologies which will arrive in the next years. The deployment of occupational exoskeletons is conditioned by the regulatory frameworks and by the required reorganization of the workplace. Both concepts and the latest developments are discussed in this chapter, including their integration into Industry 4.0. Finally, this chapter describes the most common evaluation methods and discusses current efforts toward standardized benchmarking methods which will allow evaluating the benefit of using exoskeletons in real applications.

candidates.title: Blockchain Security: An Empirical Evaluation of High‐Impact Exploits and Detection Tools
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Blockchain introduced secure, peer‐to‐peer transactions in decentralized environments without reliance on central authorities. However, attackers continue to exploit blockchain projects. Over the past decade, reported blockchain exploit losses have exceeded $24 billion. Although existing research analyzes blockchain vulnerabilities and real‐world incidents, many studies focus on specific vulnerability classes or smart contract issues only. Therefore, we present an empirical study of major blockchain exploits from 2020 to 2025. Based on detailed analysis of these exploits, we introduce a practitioner‐oriented taxonomy that organizes the dominant root causes observed in the analyzed exploits across four domains: Human Risks, Off‐Chain Infrastructure Vulnerabilities, Private Key Compromises, and Smart Contract Vulnerabilities. Across these categories, we present case studies, code illustrations where applicable, and mitigation strategies. Moreover, we evaluate five vulnerability‐detection tools spanning four paradigms, namely static analysis ( Slither , 4naly3er ), symbolic execution ( Mythril ), bounded/formal verification ( SMTChecker ), and LLM‐assisted analysis ( GPTScan ), on a curated test suite of vulnerable and secure contracts. Our results show detection gaps under the evaluated setting: Slither, Mythril, and 4naly3er all scored recall below 40%. SMTChecker and GPTScan were evaluated separately because of their narrower target scopes. SMTChecker detected only arithmetic issues, while GPTScan produced no benchmark‐relevant detections. The study highlights the high average loss associated with smart contract access‐control failures, the need for post‐deployment monitoring beyond one‐time audits, and risks related to Off‐Chain Infrastructure Vulnerabilities. By analyzing exploits and offering mitigations, we provide a structured reference for identifying, prioritizing, and mitigating major blockchain security risks.

candidates.title: AI Companions and Loneliness: Conceptualizing and Operationalizing Synthetic Mindfulness and Exploring Its Role in Alleviating Loneliness
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT The rise of AI companions has sparked interest in their potential to alleviate the growing social problem of loneliness, yet evidence of their effectiveness remains unsettled. Drawing on social surrogacy theory with a theories‐in‐use approach, this research introduces synthetic mindfulness, defined as consumers' judgment of an AI companion's capacity to maintain an attentive presence, engage in a non‐judgmental way, and respond with sensitive attunement to their needs. We argue that these judgments shape whether consumers experience AI companions as capable of reducing their loneliness. Across one qualitative and four quantitative studies, we develop and validate a three‐dimensional measure of synthetic mindfulness. Our final study demonstrates that higher judgments of synthetic mindfulness reduce loneliness via consumers' strengthened sense of belonging and self‐esteem. This research advances understanding of how AI companions can effectively address loneliness and provides a conceptual foundation for examining synthetic mindfulness in human–AI relationships.

candidates.title: SPREAD, a framework and open-source R toolbox to quantify behavioural contagion
candidates.abstract: Behavioural contagion, when one individual's behaviour increases the likelihood of similar behaviours in others, is a fundamental dimension of social interaction, yet its empirical quantification remains methodologically challenging. Distinguishing contagion from coincidental co-occurrence, resolving contagion across continuous latencies rather than within fixed windows, accounting for behavioural base rates, and incorporating social structure require integrated analytical solutions. We present SPREAD, a conceptual and statistical framework implemented as an open-source R toolbox for quantifying behavioural contagion in time-series interaction data. SPREAD compares observed behavioural sequences with null distributions generated from permuted data that preserve individual event frequencies while disrupting inter-individual temporal alignment. The framework yields latency-resolved, base-rate corrected estimates of contagion strength that are comparable across behaviours and social configurations. We demonstrate SPREAD across two behavioural domains, laughter and eating, using human triadic data and illustrate its ability to detect contagion effects across distinct temporal dynamics.

candidates.title: Ritual Paraphernalia Toward a Modular Approach to Coptic Magic
candidates.abstract: This article explores the redactional strategies through which ritual experts in late antique and early medieval Egypt articulated their textual products. It adopts what is here heuristically termed a ‘modular approach’, which treats magical texts as assemblages of discrete textual segments that could be extracted, recombined, and adapted to different redactional agendas. Drawing on selected case studies from Coptic ritual manuscripts, the article offers a new model for understanding scribal practice and the transmission of ritual knowledge.

candidates.title: Intelligent Mechatronics: intelligence in the design process, not only the machine
candidates.abstract: Designing a physical machine requires mechanical, electronic, control, and software decisions to be settled together, each constraining the others, under the standards governing the environment it will work in. This reasoning is held by experienced engineers and rarely written down. That, I argue, is why artificial intelligence has reached the design of software but not of the machines that software runs on. Physical design is, in part, genuinely harder, and its errors are costly and irreversible, but that is not the whole explanation. Software’s design reasoning was written down alongside the public code that an AI could learn from; the knowledge that conceives and sizes a physical system was not. As the design bottleneck shifts to physical systems, intelligence must be applied to the design process itself, not only to the product. Taking mechatronics as the case, I find that where its defining sources invoke intelligence at all, it is for the product or the discipline that builds it, never for the process that designs it. The capture of tacit, cross-domain design knowledge in a form that AI can use is a binding constraint on AI-assisted physical design, and the most neglected as well. A three-layer model locates it: Layer 1, this design knowledge is the missing foundation; the AI reasoning and agent layers above advance rapidly but cannot design physical systems without it. The physical machine and its intelligent twin are developed together from this foundation. A worked design-rationale analysis of an offshore-crane actuation decision grounds what Layer 1 must hold: the rationale residue that existing formats do not capture. In this article, I set out a research agenda, from capturing this knowledge to generalizing beyond mechatronics, and state the conditions under which its central claim would fail.

candidates.title: Steel robots and space turtleships: the divergence of Korean animation and Japanese anime
candidates.abstract: During the Park Chung-hee military dictatorship, Korea shadowed Japanese industrial upgrading at every stage. The same was true in animation, in which Korea took Japanese animations, indigenized them, and imbued them with a techno-nationalism that positioned Korean animation as both dependent on Japan and destined to overcome it. Instead, the opposite happened: today South Korean animation is a pale shadow of Japanese anime’s global success. This essay argues that this divergence, rather than the result of flawed state policies or overdependence on outsourcing, is the result of objective shifts in global capitalism that began in the 1970s. This essay analyses two Korean animated films that mimicked Japanese animated works: Robot Taekwon V (1976), which mimicked Japanese animated film Mazinger Z (1972) and Fly! Spaceship Geobukseon (1979), which mimicked TV series and film Space Battleship Yamato (1974–1975; 1977). While the former Japan-Korea couplet was situated in convergence between the HCI (heavy and chemical industry) economic plans of Japan and Korea, the latter couplet marked the divergence between Korean animation and Japanese ‘anime,’ i.e. the rise of a new commodity form constituted by global ‘otaku’ consumption that reshaped the global economy and ended the previous period’s possibility of economic development.
